## E1010 POWER SUPPLY SYSTEM - DESCRIPTION  [939011443]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E10 POWER SUPPLY AND EARTHS > E1010 POWER SUPPLY > E1010 POWER SUPPLY SYSTEM - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011443

#### DESCRIPTION
The electrical system is designed to increase the car's safety level and prevent the possibility of fires and other consequences of electrical malfunctions. State-of-the-art connectors have been introduced to rule out the possibility of many connection defects.
Power is distributed via the junction units and/ or fuses boxes. These are connected to control elements (relays and static actuators) to ensure maximum electrical protection and minimum wiring complexity.
All wiring looms have been made modular (sub-assembly composition) by changing the way functions are distributed inside the connectors and replacing welds with short-circuiting joints.
The main safety solutions adopted are as follows:
- power supplies protected by maxi fuses to cut off the electrical system in the event of a short circuit (see detail below);
- the only cables not fitted with maxi fuses (starter motor and alternator) are armoured and located in protected areas. In the event of an emergency - operation of the inertia switch - these cables are disconnected by an automatic device located in the battery fuse box
See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING [→939011733]
- the layout of the whole system is optimised to reduce the risk of damage in the event of faults or accidents;
- wiring installation has been optimised to reduced incorrect positioning and noise due to vibrations
- all wires offer high resistance to abrasion;
- the wires in the engine are specially designed to be resistant to high temperatures and are protected by outer casings or piping;
- the wires in the passenger compartment are protected by corrugated pipes and napped tape to reduce noise levels;
- the main connections come with secondary lock terminals and lever locks or "CPA" to prevent terminal deformation.
All systems and electrical equipment are supplied by the battery at a voltage of 12V.
The battery is recharged by the alternator during engine operation
See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING [→939011733]
The main power supply lines are protected by MAXI FUSES housed in the engine compartment junction unit; other shunt fuses are located outside it.
> Note: This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key where the traditional ignition key has been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G." (Transmitter for Entry and go) combined with an electronic key reader and TEG-Reader radio frequency receiver.
Some circuits are continuously supplied, even with the car at a standstill and the TEG extracted, because they are connected directly to the battery.
Other circuits are supplied with the TEG inserted in the TEG Reader: the distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (INT and 15/54, INT/A, "AVV", etc.) is managed by the "steering lock node", and takes place in exactly the same way as on models with a traditional key.
> Note: The lines that distribute power to the various appliances are represented by wiring diagrams for the various functions and systems.This general diagram shows all the lines as they leave the battery and maxi fuse boxes. Refer to specific diagrams for more details.

## E1010 POWER SUPPLY SYSTEM - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011444]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E10 POWER SUPPLY AND EARTHS > E1010 POWER SUPPLY > E1010 POWER SUPPLY SYSTEM - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011444

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
All electrical systems and circuits are supplied by battery A1.
The main power supply lines are protected by maxi fuses in the maxi fuse box on the battery B99, in particular:
- CVM: engine compartment junction unit B1 power supply - connector X;
- CPL: junction unit under the dashboard B2 power supply - to pin A of connector C;
- CPR : glowplugs control unit power supply (for Diesel engines only)
See E5050 DIESEL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT [→939003133]
The B99 fuse box includes the automatic battery disconnection device which, in emergencies, cuts off the power supply to the engine starting/ recharging cable.
See descriptions 5530 CURRENT GENERATION [→939003531 5530 CURRENT GENERATION]
For Diesel engines only, there is an additional fuse box B98, next to the maxi fuse box on the battery (on one side of the battery itself), equipped with two MIDI maxi fuses which supply the additional heater.
See E6015 ADDITIONAL HEATER [→939003163]
The following, amongst others, are supplied by the engine compartment junction unit B1:
- the steering lock node M89 (which "replaces" the ignition switch), fuse F3;
- the junction unit under the dashboard B2 and the one in the luggage compartment B45 fuse F1.
The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (INT ignition-operated, 15/54, INT/A, "AVV", etc.) is managed by the steering lock control unit, and takes place in exactly the same way as on models with a traditional key.
The power supply for the M89 control unit reaches pin C1 of M89 from the line protected by fuse F3 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 whilst pin A4 of M89 is earthed.
The TEG inserted status is sent by the TEG Reader H3 via the CAN - pins 3 and 8. The same signal is sent, redundantly, to the steering lock node M89, from pin 2 and the latter, in turn, forwards it via the CAN.
With the TEG inserted, numerous ignition-operated circuits and services are supplied (lines INT and 15/54): lines leaving pins A1 and B1 of M89.
With the TEG inserted, without starting up (INT/A line): other circuits and services are supplied: from pins B3 and C8 of M89.

#### DESCRIPTION
The following diagram shows the various earths on the car. The associated circuits are shown for each earth.
This makes it easy to identify the earthed circuits on an individual line: faults and failures are therefore easier to locate in the case of problems that affect more than one function: for example, oxidation of an earth may put several circuits and numerous functions out of service simultaneously.

## E1020 EARTHS - OPERATIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939003391]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E10 POWER SUPPLY AND EARTHS > E1020 EARTHS > E1020 EARTHS - OPERATIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; period: From 01/06
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939003391

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The earths present on the vehicle, categorised according to their relationship with the various wires, are as follows.
Radiator wiring:
- battery earth, C01 A
Front wiring:
- left front earth, C10
- right front earth, C11
- ABS front earth (on left corner), C12
- earth on engine, C40
Dashboard wiring:
- passenger side facia earth, C20
- Air Bag system earth, C50 A
Rear wiring:
- driver's dashboard earth, C 15
- left rear earth, C30
- right rear earth, C31
- heated rear windscreen earth, C32
- Air Bag system earth, C50 B
Battery negative wiring:
- battery earth on engine (on gearbox), C02
- battery earth on bodyshell, C03 A, C03 B
Engine wiring:
- earth on engine, C40 B, C40 C, (petrol engine only)
- compressor earth, C39 (only engine 3.2 V6 version)
HIFI amplifier wiring:
- earth for amplifier, C56
Air conditioning wiring:
- air conditioning unit earth, C16

## E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES - DESCRIPTION  [939011453]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E10 POWER SUPPLY AND EARTHS > E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES > E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011453

#### DESCRIPTION
This vehicle is equipped with a CAN (Controller Area Network) system of electrical connections: it involves a software and hardware solution which is designed to manage the resources on the vehicle efficiently allowing:
- the sharing of information between the various electronic units;
- the intergration of several electronic units through one network;
- a high network information exchange speed;
- advantages in economic terms because there is a considerable reduction in the wiring/connectors inside the vehicle;
- higher standards in terms of quality and reliability.
The advantage of using a CAN system stems from the fact that communication takes place between numerous control units and consequently the number of signals to be managed is very high.
For this reason the signals travel on a CAN type serial Bus where one wire is high level (H) and the other low level (L); these signals on the CAN Bus are differential types, i.e. the value assigned to the bit is represented by the difference between the CAN-H and CAN-L voltage levels.
The different electronic units which make up the system, known as network nodes, are connected to the CAN by means of communication interfaces known as transreceivers; these connection interfaces, integrated in the electronic units, constitute the gate for sending/reading the information at the CAN or at the serial lines.
The exchange of information at CAN type serial lines is only possible using a transmission protocol which is the collection of rules that allow communication between two or more nodes by means of the exchange of information or "data packages".
The main element of the network is the Body Computer.
The Body Computer node is entrusted with "waking up the network" when a "known" TEG is inserted in the TEG Reader (if there is a problem with the Body Computer this task is entrusted to the instrument panel).
The Body Computer also carries out the network checking functions which make it possible to provide information on:
- the network activities status;
- the functional failure status of the individual electronic units (nodes);
- a possible CAN fault.
The various electronic units process the various signals coming from the corresponding sensors both for their own management and for other control units to which they are sent via the CAN.
The specific structure adopted for this vehicle consists of two CAN communication networks which connect nodes belonging to two different areas:
- C-CAN for dynamic vehicle control (high speed): bus CAN-H and CAN-L;
- B-CAN for the management of standard body functions (low speed): bus CAN-A and CAN-B;
the two CAN communication networks are connected to one another by a gateway for transferring joint information, located in the Body Computer Node.
The fault diagnosis of the nodes connected to the B-CAN network is carried out via the CAN network, whilst for those connected to the C-CAN this is carried out by means of the specific K lines.
See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR [→939011851]
There is also the W line, ISO 5 serial for recovery of the Code system
See E7010 CODE [→939011820]
and the A-BUS serial line ISO 5 for the alarm, wiping functions, lighting, tyre pressure monitoring system.
See E1060 A-BUS SERIAL LINE [→939011457]
Power is distributed via the junction units and/ or fuses boxes. These are connected to control elements (relays and static actuators) to ensure maximum electrical protection and minimum wiring complexity.
See E1010 POWER SUPPLY [→939011442]

## E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011454]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E10 POWER SUPPLY AND EARTHS > E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES > E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011454

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The Body Computer M1 is supplied directly from the battery via line protected by maxifuse F1 of engine compartment control unit B1 at pin 18 of connector F that interfaces with underfacia control unit B2 .
The Body Computer M1 receives an ignition-operated supply (INT) at pin 9 of connector F of the interface with the junction unit under the dashboard B2 : this signal is used, amongst other things, to "wake up the network".
Pins 8 and 9 of connector I of M1 are earthed.
The nodes connected to Body Computer M1 - from pins 36 and 37 of connector B - via the high speed C-CAN network are:
- engine management control unit M10;
- ABS/VDC control unit M50 ;
- automatic transmission control unit M55 (only on version with Automatic Transmission);
- gear selector control unit M53 (only on version with Automatic Transmission);
- steering angle sensor K58 (only present on versions with VDC);
- slewing sensor K74 (only present on versions with VDC);
The following nodes are connected to the Body Computer M1 via the B-CAN low speed network:
- underfacia junction unit B2 ;
- instrument panel E50;
- driver's side door control unit M66 , passenger side door M67 ;
- boot compartment control unit M63 ;
- parking sensor control unit M84 ;
- seat control unit H66 and H67;
- Air Bag control unit M60 .
- climate control sytem control unit M70;
- controls on the steering wheel (via the clock spring D47);
- built-in radio-telephone-navigator P20;
- Bluetooth control unit M162
- steering lock control unit M89 ;
- TEG Reader H3.

## E1060 A - BUS SERIAL LINE - DESCRIPTION  [939011458]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E10 POWER SUPPLY AND EARTHS > E1060 A-BUS SERIAL LINE > E1060 A - BUS SERIAL LINE - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011458

#### DESCRIPTION
This vehicle is equipped with a CAN (Controller Area Network) system of electrical connections.
The different electronic units that make up the system, known as network "Nodes" are connected to the CAN; the main element of the network is the Body Computer.
The various electronic units process the various signals coming from the corresponding sensors both for their own management and for other control units to which they are sent via the CAN.
The structure consists of two CAN communication networks which connect nodes belonging to two different areas:
- C-CAN for dynamic vehicle control (high speed): bus CAN-H and CAN-L;
- B-CAN for the management of standard body functions (low speed): bus CAN-A and CAN-B;
the two CAN communication networks are connected to one another by a gateway for transferring joint information, located in the Body Computer Node.
See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES [→939011452]
A special A-BUS ISO 5 serial line manages the connection with the following functions:
- alarm (siren and volumetric/anti-tilt sensors);
- automatic wiping (rain senosr);
- automatic lighting (dusk sensor).

## E1060 A - BUS SERIAL LINE - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011459]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E10 POWER SUPPLY AND EARTHS > E1060 A-BUS SERIAL LINE > E1060 A - BUS SERIAL LINE - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011459

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The Body Computer M1 is supplied directly from the battery via line protected by maxifuse F1 of engine compartment control unit B1 at pin 18 of connector F that interfaces with underfacia control unit B2 .
The Body Computer M1 receives an ignition-operated supply (INT) at pin 9 of connector F of the interface with the junction unit under the dashboard B2 : this signal is used, amongst other things, to "wake up the network".
Pins 8 and 9 of connector I of M1 are earthed.
The A-BUS serial line is connected from pin 25 of connector B of the Body Computer M1 with the alarm sensor P90 - pin 2 - and with th steering column switch unit H5 - pin 2 of connector A; the latter manages the signal from the rain sensor.
The A-BUS serial line is connected from pin 7 of connector D of the Body Computer M1 with the volumetric/anti-tilt sensors, located in the courtesy light G10 - connector C - pin 4 - and with the rain and dusk sensors, incorporated in the electro-chromic interior rear view mirror P65, pin 3.

## E2010 SIDE LIGHTS/NUMBER PLATE LIGHT - DESCRIPTION  [939011469]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS > E2010 SIDE LIGHTS/NUMBER PLATE LIGHT - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Xenon Gas headlamps
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011469

#### DESCRIPTION
The side lights are switched on at the first turn of the ring nut on the left steering column switch unit lever. The turning on of the side lights is managed by the Body Computer.
The side lights control function is activated through the TEG on enablement signals (INT) and the command from the steering column switch unit: the four side lights are supplied in this way.
The number plate light and numerous other interior lights for lighting the passenger compartment, instruments and controls are activated together with the side lights (these are described and explained in the wiring diagrams for the relevant components).
Activation/deactivation information is sent via the CAN network: in this way, the side lights warning light in the instrument panel is also activated. The instrument panel also activates the nightime lighting.
The side lights can be activated automatically by means of the dusk sensor if the AUTO function is set on the steering column switch unit. The dusk sensor is an infrared device that operates at different sensitivity settings: when the dusk sensor is activated a message is shown on the instrument panel display indicating the sensitivity setting (from 1 to 3): this setting can be adjusted using the "Mode +" and "Mode -" buttons.
The "parking lights" function is turned on - only with the TEG extracted - by pressing the button in the panel to the left of the steering wheel: a roger beep signals engagement. If the steering column switch unit left lever is turned (in the same way as for activating the direction indicators) it is possible to choose whether to turn on the side lights on both sides of the vehicle (lever in middle position) or only those on one side (lever downwards to select the left side, lever upwards to select the right side).
The "Follow me home" function allows the dipped headlamps and the side lights to remain on even after the engine has been switched off (TEG extracted) for a period of 30 seconds or multiples thereof. The side lights warning light in the instrument panel signals that the lights have remained on. It is turned on using the lever in the same way as for activating the flasher within 2 minutes of the TEG being extracted: each time the lever is operated the time the lights remain on is increased by 30 seconds up to a maximum of 210 seconds. If the TEG is inserted or the flasher lever is pulled for more than 2 seconds, the function is excluded.
The correct operation of the lights is checked by the side lights and no. plate lights check function: the following is checked for each of the circuits:
- circuit open or bulb missing
- short-circuit to earth (bulb s.c. or wiring s.c. to earth)
- short circuit to battery voltage (wiring short circuited to Vbatt)
When one of the situations described above is ascertained, the Body Computer makes the failure status available to the CAN: a special "lights failure" warning light comes on in the instrument panel and, at the same time, the information is shown in the display.
For safe driving, if there is a fault with one of the rear bulbs, with the side lights on the brake light bulb on the corresponding side comes on dimly to simulate the brightness of the side light. The system also detects any faults in the dusk sensor: if a fault is detected, the "general failure" warning light is turned on and the information is shown simultaneously on the display.

## E2010 SIDE LIGHTS/NUMBER PLATE LIGHT - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011470]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS > E2010 SIDE LIGHTS/NUMBER PLATE LIGHT - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Xenon Gas headlamps
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011470

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
Two signals (earth) are sent from the steering wheel stalk unit H5 to the Body Computer M1 that manages both side lights and low beams in manual or AUTO mode (automatic dusk sensor activation).
The "Light 1" signal - is sent to pin 28 of connector G of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unit H5, pin 7 of connector C. The "Light 2" signal - is sent to pin 2 of connector I of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unig H5, pin 8 of connector C. The side lights are turned on manually when the "Light 1" signal is missing and the "Light 2" signal is present.
The side lights are activated in AUTO mode when the Light 1 signal is not present and the Light 2 signal is not present. If both signals are present, the lights are permanently off.
The side lights are automatically activated by the dusk sensor housed in the mirror P65 (signal via the A-BUS line to pin 7 of connector D of M1); the dusk sensor in P65 receives a supply from the INT line protected by fuse F49 of junction unit B2.
The lights are also activated by the parking lights button located in the left switch unit H90 which sends an earth signal to pin 17 of connector H of M1.
The Body Computer M1 controls the supply for the front side lights F10 (left) and F11 (right) from pins 40 and 30 of connector B, for the rear side lights F30 and F35 (left), F31 and F36 (right) and the number plate lights F50 and F51 from pins 5, 6, 9 of connector D and 38 of connector E.
Via the CAN line, the Body Computer M1 is connected to instrument panel E50 to manage the side lights on warning light and, if faults are detected in the circuit or in the bulbs, the lights failure warning light; in the vent of a fault with the dusk sensor there is a specific signal.

## E2010 SIDE LIGHTS/NUMBER PLATE LIGHT - DESCRIPTION  [939005479]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS > E2010 SIDE LIGHTS/NUMBER PLATE LIGHT - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Station Wagon, Xenon Gas headlamps
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939005479

#### DESCRIPTION
The side lights are switched on at the first turn of the ring nut on the left steering column switch unit lever. The turning on of the side lights is managed by the Body Computer.
The side lights control function is activated through the TEG on enablement signals (INT) and the command from the steering column switch unit: the four side lights are supplied in this way.
The number plate light and numerous other interior lights for lighting the passenger compartment, instruments and controls are activated together with the side lights (these are described and explained in the wiring diagrams for the relevant components).
Activation/deactivation information is sent via the CAN network: in this way, the side lights warning light in the instrument panel is also activated. The instrument panel also activates the nightime lighting.
The side lights can be activated automatically by means of the dusk sensor if the AUTO function is set on the steering column switch unit. The dusk sensor is an infrared device that operates at different sensitivity settings: when the dusk sensor is activated a message is shown on the instrument panel display indicating the sensitivity setting (from 1 to 3): this setting can be adjusted using the "Mode +" and "Mode -" buttons.
The "parking lights" function is turned on - only with the TEG extracted - by pressing the button in the panel to the left of the steering wheel: a roger beep signals engagement. If the steering column switch unit left lever is turned (in the same way as for activating the direction indicators) it is possible to choose whether to turn on the side lights on both sides of the vehicle (lever in middle position) or only those on one side (lever downwards to select the left side, lever upwards to select the right side).
The "Follow me home" function allows the dipped headlamps and the side lights to remain on even after the engine has been switched off (TEG extracted) for a period of 30 seconds or multiples thereof. The side lights warning light in the instrument panel signals that the lights have remained on. It is turned on using the lever in the same way as for activating the flasher within 2 minutes of the TEG being extracted: each time the lever is operated the time the lights remain on is increased by 30 seconds up to a maximum of 210 seconds. If the TEG is inserted or the flasher lever is pulled for more than 2 seconds, the function is excluded.
The correct operation of the lights is checked by the side lights and no. plate lights check function: the following is checked for each of the circuits:
- circuit open or bulb missing
- short-circuit to earth (bulb s.c. or wiring s.c. to earth)
- short circuit to battery voltage (wiring short circuited to Vbatt)
When one of the situations described above is ascertained, the Body Computer makes the failure status available to the CAN: a special "lights failure" warning light comes on in the instrument panel and, at the same time, the information is shown in the display.
For safe driving, if there is a fault with one of the rear bulbs, with the side lights on the brake light bulb on the corresponding side comes on dimly to simulate the brightness of the side light. The system also detects any faults in the dusk sensor: if a fault is detected, the "general failure" warning light is turned on and the information is shown simultaneously on the display.

## E2010 SIDE LIGHTS/NUMBER PLATE LIGHT - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939005480]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS > E2010 SIDE LIGHTS/NUMBER PLATE LIGHT - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Station Wagon, Xenon Gas headlamps
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939005480

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
Two signals (earth) are sent from the steering wheel stalk unit H5 to the Body Computer M1 that manages both side lights and low beams in manual or AUTO mode (automatic dusk sensor activation).
The "Light 1" signal - is sent to pin 28 of connector G of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unit H5, pin 7 of connector C. The "Light 2" signal - is sent to pin 2 of connector I of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unig H5, pin 8 of connector C. The side lights are turned on manually when the "Light 1" signal is missing and the "Light 2" signal is present.
The side lights are activated in AUTO mode when the Light 1 signal is not present and the Light 2 signal is not present. If both signals are present, the lights are permanently off.
The side lights are automatically activated by the dusk sensor housed in the mirror P65 (signal via the A-BUS line to pin 7 of connector D of M1); the dusk sensor in P65 receives a supply from the INT line protected by fuse F49 of junction unit B2.
The lights are also activated by the parking lights button located in the left switch unit H90 which sends an earth signal to pin 17 of connector H of M1.
The Body Computer M1 controls the supply for the front side lights F10 (left) and F11 (right) from pins 40 and 30 of connector B, for the rear side lights F30 and F35 (left), F31 and F36 (right) and the number plate lights F50 and F51 from pins 5, 6, 9 of connector D and 38 of connector E.
Via the CAN line, the Body Computer M1 is connected to instrument panel E50 to manage the side lights on warning light and, if faults are detected in the circuit or in the bulbs, the lights failure warning light; in the vent of a fault with the dusk sensor there is a specific signal.

## E2011 DIPPED HEADLIGHTS - DESCRIPTION  [939011479]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS > E2011 DIPPED HEADLIGHTS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Xenon Gas headlamps
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011479

#### DESCRIPTION
The vehicle is fitted with two GAS DISCHARGE headlamps.
The electronics built into each of the two headlamps switch them on and off according to the times defined by the software and, in accordance with international regulations, the gas discharge bulbs too. The system comprises an igniter located in the base of the bulb and a ballast located in the bottom part of the lamp.
The left lamp is the master control unit, whilst the right one performs a slave role.
The master lamp acquires the command for the dipped headlamps, the vehicle speed and from the potentiometers located on the wheel axles. Depending on the inputs, it directly controls the switching on of the left front headlamp (dipped headlamps) and controls the right one in a similar way via the serial line.
The dipped beams are activated by turning a wheel on the stalk switch to the next position after the side light setting.
A relay in the underfacia control unit controls activation of the low beams via two lines protected by specific fuses.
The low beam activation relay is controlled by the Body Computer relay energizing is activated by enablement signals with the TEG inserted (INT) and from the specific signal from the steering column switch unit.
With the dipped headlamps on, the switching to main beams causes the shutter in gas discharge bulb to be raised with a switch to main beams.
The dipped headlamps can be automatically activated by means of the dusk sensor, if the AUTO function is set on the steering column switch unit. The dusk sensor is an infrared device that works at different sensitivity settings: when the dusk sensor is activated a message is shown on the instrument panel display indicating the sensitivity setting (from 1 to 3): this setting can be adjusted using the "Mode +" and "Mode -" buttons.
The "Follow me home" function allows the dipped headlamps and the side lights to remain on even after the engine has been switched off (TEG extracted) for a period of 30 seconds or multiples thereof. The "dipped headlamps" warning light in the instrument panel signals that the lights have remained on.
It is turned on using the lever in the same way as for activating the flasher within 2 minutes of the TEG being extracted: each time the lever is operated the length of time the lights remain on is increased by 30 seconds, up to a maximum of 210 seconds. Inserting the TEG or keeping the flasher lever pulled for more than 2 seconds eliminates the function.

## E2011 DIPPED HEADLIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011480]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS > E2011 DIPPED HEADLIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Xenon Gas headlamps
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011480

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
Two signals (earth) are sent from the steering wheel stalk unit H5 to the Body Computer M1 that manages both side lights and low beams in manual or AUTO mode (automatic dusk sensor activation).
The "Light 1" signal is sent from pin 28 of connector G of Body Computer M1 from stalk unit H5, pin 7 of connector C.
The "Light 2" signal is sent to pin 2 of connector I of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unit H5, pin 8 of connector C. The dipped headlamps are switched on manually when the "Light 1" is absent and when the "Light 2" signal is also missing.
The dipped headlamps are activated in AUTO mode when the Light 1 signal is present and the Light 2 signal is not present. If both signals are present, the lights are constantly off.
The dipped headlamps are automatically activated by the dusk sensor housed in the mirror P65 (signal via the A-BUS line at pin 7 of connector D of M1); the dusk sensor in P65 receives a supply from the INT line protected by fuse F49 of junction unit B2.
The Body Computer M1 controls the supply for the dipped headlamps sending an earth signal to relay T1 in the junction unit under the dashboard B2 from pin 8 of connector F of M1 which energizes relay T1: this supplies the dipped headlamps F10 (left) and F11 (right). Each circuit is protected by a fuse in the junction unit B2 : F13 for the left headlamp and F12 for the right.
Both electronic systems inside the headlamps F10 (left) and F11 (right) are supplied - pin 9 - from the INT line of junction unit B2 protected by fuse F37.
Pins 12 of the two control units are connected to one another by means of a special serial line, whilst the speedometer signal from the Body Computer M1 (pin 28 of connector B) reaches pin 10 of the junction unit located in headlamp F10.
Pins 11 of the two headlamps are connected to the diagnostic K line
See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR [→939011851]
The Body Computer M1 is connected via the CAN line to the instrument panel E50 to manage the "dipped headlamps on" warning light and, if there are problems detected in the circuit, the specific warning light.

## E2011 DIPPED HEADLIGHTS - DESCRIPTION  [939011474]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS > E2011 DIPPED HEADLIGHTS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011474

#### DESCRIPTION
The vehicle is equipped with two dipped headlamps in the lights. The headlamps are switched on by the steering column switch unit by turning the ring nut to the position after the side lights.
A special relay, located in the junciton unit under the dashboard, controls the engagement of the dipped headlamps via two lines protected by special fuses. The relay for engaging the dipped headlamps is managed by the Body Computer. relay energizing is activated by enablement signals with the TEG inserted (INT) and from the specific signal from the steering column switch unit.
With the dipped headlamps on, the simultaneous presence of the main beam and fog lights commands disables the dipped headlamps. The subsequent deactivation of one of these two commands, with the dipped headlamps control still on, involves the dipped headlamps being turned back on.
The dipped headlamps can be automatically activated by means of the dusk sensor, if the AUTO function is set on the steering column switch unit. The dusk sensor is an infrared device that works at different sensitivity settings: when the dusk sensor is activated a message is shown on the instrument panel display indicating the sensitivity setting (from 1 to 3): this setting can be adjusted using the "Mode +" and "Mode -" buttons.
The "Follow me home" function allows the dipped headlamps and the side lights to remain on even after the engine has been switched off (TEG extracted) for a period of 30 seconds or multiples thereof. The "dipped headlamps" warning light in the instrument panel signals that the lights have remained on.
It is turned on using the lever in the same way as for activating the flasher within 2 minutes of the TEG being extracted: each time the lever is operated the length of time the lights remain on is increased by 30 seconds, up to a maximum of 210 seconds. Inserting the TEG or keeping the flasher lever pulled for more than 2 seconds eliminates the function.

## E2012 MAIN BEAM HEADLIGHTS - DESCRIPTION  [939011489]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2012 MAIN BEAM HEADLAMPS > E2012 MAIN BEAM HEADLIGHTS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Xenon Gas headlamps
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011489

#### DESCRIPTION
If the vehicle is equipped with GAS DISCHARGE headlamps, there are two main beams: the first is a specific SPOT light, the second a gas discharge bulb that lights up like a full beam once the shutter for the dipped beam mode is raised.
The main beams are switched on by the steering column switch unit:
- with the dipped beams on, by pushing the lever towards the dashboard (stable mode)
- in flashing mode, by pulling the lever toward the steering wheel (unstable mode)
The switching between the dipped beam and main beam functions for xenon bulbs causes the raising of the shutter in the gas discharge bulb, with the switch to the main beam; at the same time, the main beam SPOT light also comes on. The spot light main beam comes on by itself through the flasher control (unstable mode) with the main beams switched off.
The low beam activation relay is controlled by the Body Computer relay energizing is activated by enablement signals with the TEG inserted (INT) and from the specific signal from the steering column switch unit.
Activation/deactivation information is sent via the CAN network: in this way, the main beam warning light is activated in the instrument panel.
> Note: for legal reasons, if the dusk sensor is activated, only the flasher can be operated and the main beams cannot be turned on permanently; the AUTO function must be switched off in order to activate these lights.

## E2012 MAIN BEAM HEADLIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011490]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2012 MAIN BEAM HEADLAMPS > E2012 MAIN BEAM HEADLIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Xenon Gas headlamps
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011490

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The dipped headlamps (earth) activation signal (stable mode) is sent to pin 4 of connector I of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unit H5; the flasher activation (earth) signal (unstable mode) is, on the other hand, sent to pin 33 of connector G of the Body Computer M1.
The Body Computer M1 controls the supply for the dipped headlamps sending an earth signal to relay T2 in the junction unit in the engine compartment B1 from pin 9 of connector A of M1 which energizes relay T2: this supplies the dipped headlamps F10 (left) and F11 (right). Each circuit is protected by a fuse in the junction unit B1 : F15 for the left headlamp and F14 for the right.
Both electronic systems inside the headlamps F10 (left) and F11 (right) are supplied - pin 9 - from the INT line of junction unit B2 protected by fuse F37.
Pins 12 of the two control units are connected to one another by means of a special serial line, whilst the speedometer signal from the Body Computer M1 (pin 28 of connector B) reaches pin 10 of the junction unit located in headlamp F10.
Pins 11 of the two headlamps are connected to the diagnostic K line
See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR [→939011851]
The Body Computer M1 is connected via the CAN line to the instrument panel E50 to manage the "main beam headlamps" warning light.

## E2012 MAIN BEAM HEADLIGHTS - DESCRIPTION  [939011484]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2012 MAIN BEAM HEADLAMPS > E2012 MAIN BEAM HEADLIGHTS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011484

#### DESCRIPTION
The vehicle is equipped with two high beams in the headlamps.
The main beams are switched on by the steering column switch unit:
- with the dipped beams on, by pushing the lever towards the dashboard (stable mode)
- in flashing mode, by pulling the lever toward the steering wheel (unstable mode)
The low beam activation relay is controlled by the Body Computer relay energizing is activated by enablement signals with the TEG inserted (INT) and from the specific signal from the steering column switch unit.
Activation/deactivation information is sent via the CAN network: in this way, the main beam warning light is activated in the instrument panel.
> Note: for legal reasons, if the dusk sensor is activated, only the flasher can be operated and the main beams cannot be turned on permanently; the AUTO function must be switched off in order to activate these lights.

## E2012 MAIN BEAM HEADLIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011485]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2012 MAIN BEAM HEADLAMPS > E2012 MAIN BEAM HEADLIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011485

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The dipped headlamps (earth) activation signal (stable mode) is sent to pin 4 of connector I of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unit H5; the flasher activation (earth) signal (unstable mode) is, on the other hand, sent to pin 33 of connector G of the Body Computer M1.
The Body Computer M1 controls the supply for the dipped headlamps sending an earth signal to relay T2 in the junction unit in the engine compartment B1 from pin 9 of connector A of M1 which energizes relay T2: this supplies the dipped headlamps F10 (left) and F11 (right). Each circuit is protected by a fuse in the junction unit B1 : F15 for the left headlamp and F14 for the right.
The Body Computer M1 is connected via the CAN line to the instrument panel E50 to manage the "main beam headlamps" warning light.

## E2020 DIRECTION INDICATORS/HAZARD WARNING LIGHTS - DESCRIPTION  [939011499]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2020 DIRECTION INDICATORS / HAZARD WARNING LIGHTS > E2020 DIRECTION INDICATORS/HAZARD WARNING LIGHTS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Xenon Gas headlamps
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011499

#### DESCRIPTION
The left and right direction indicators are switched on by raising or lowering the special lever on the left of the steering column switch unit; the function is activated with the TEG inserted (ON).
The hazard warning lights (left and right direction indicators operated simultaneously) are activated via a button in the centre console next to the gear lever and activates all the direction indicators simultaneously. An LED at the back of the control button also comes on synchronized with the flashing of the exterior lights. This function is always activated for safety reasons.
The engagement of the direction indicators / hazard warning lights is managed by the Body Computer which also controls the flashing frequency which is sent to the other nodes via the CAN serial network. In this way the two direction indicator warning lights in the instrument panel are also switched on; in addition, the system provides a low frequency acoustic signal in conjunction with the activation of the lights.
The direction indicators check function checks that the lights are working properly: the following are checked for each of the two circuit (right side branch and vehicle left side):
- circuit open or bulb missing
- short-circuit to earth (bulb s.c. or wiring s.c. to earth)
- short circuit to battery voltage (wiring short circuited to Vbatt)
When one of the situations described above is ascertained, the Body Computer makes the failure status available to the CAN: in the instrument panel: a special failure warning light comes on and, at the same time, the information is shown in the display only at the key on.
In addition, at the same time as a failure warning light comes on, the flashing frequency of the visual indication in the display and the acoustic signal increases; the flashing frequency of the exterior lights and the LED in the emergency button, on the other hand, remains unchanged.
> Note: the direction indicators are also used to signal that the commands sent by the remote control have been received and/or to signal a manoeuvre not carried out by the "passenger compartment access" control system.See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING [→939003023]

## E2020 DIRECTION INDICATORS/HAZARD WARNING LIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011500]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2020 DIRECTION INDICATORS / HAZARD WARNING LIGHTS > E2020 DIRECTION INDICATORS/HAZARD WARNING LIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Xenon Gas headlamps
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011500

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The direction indicator (earth) activation signals are sent to pins 7 of connector I and 30 of connector G of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unit H5.
The hazard light activation signal (earth) reaches pin 34 of connector G of M1 from control button H20.
The Body Computer M1 receives a specific direct power supply for the hazard warning lights via the line for fuse F53 of the junction unit under the dashboard B; as a result it controls the side direction indicators F20 (left) and F21 (right) from pins 2 of connector A and 22 of connector B, the sid direction indicators F10 (left) and F11 (right) from pins 38 and 39 of connector B and the rear direction indicators F30 (left) and F31 (right) from pins 12 and 3 of connector D.
A (positive) signal is sent from pin 29 of connector G of M1 to lightup the LED in the control button H20 with the power supply arriving from the INT line protected by fuse F49 of junciton unit B2.
The Body Computer M1 is connected, via the CAN line, to the instrument panel E50 to manage the "direction indicator" warning lights, the buzzer and, if there is a problem in the circuit, the "lights failure" warning light.

## E2020 DIRECTION INDICATORS/HAZARD WARNING LIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011495]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2020 DIRECTION INDICATORS / HAZARD WARNING LIGHTS > E2020 DIRECTION INDICATORS/HAZARD WARNING LIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011495

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The direction indicator (earth) activation signals are sent to pins 7 of connector I and 30 of connector G of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unit H5.
The hazard light activation signal (earth) reaches pin 34 of connector G of M1 from control button H20.
The Body Computer M1 receives a specific direct power supply for the hazard warning lights via the line for fuse F53 of the junction unit under the dashboard B; as a result it controls the side direction indicators F20 (left) and F21 (right) from pins 2 of connector A and 22 of connector B, the sid direction indicators F10 (left) and F11 (right) from pins 38 and 39 of connector B and the rear direction indicators F30 (left) and F31 (right) from pins 12 and 3 of connector D.
A (positive) signal is sent from pin 29 of connector G of M1 to lightup the LED in the control button H20 with the power supply arriving from the INT line protected by fuse F49 of junciton unit B2.
The Body Computer M1 is connected, via the CAN line, to the instrument panel E50 to manage the "direction indicator" warning lights, the buzzer and, if there is a problem in the circuit, the "lights failure" warning light.

## E2021 BRAKE LIGHTS - DESCRIPTION  [939005484]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2021 BRAKE LIGHTS > E2021 BRAKE LIGHTS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Station Wagon
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939005484

#### DESCRIPTION
The vehicle brake lights are located at the rear in the side lights (by means of a red double filament bulb together with the side light) and in the special centre third brake light mad up of 10 all glass type bulbs.
They are operated each time the brake pedal is pressed via the special switch on the actual pedal.
> Note: the switch fitted on the pedals consists of two contacts which supply two signals: the first is the N.A. type and recognizes the position of the brake pedal if it is not in the rest postion, i.e. the pedal is pressed; the second is the N.C. type and recognizes the position of the brake pedal in the rest position.The lights are turned on by the N.A. contact (pedal pressed). Information from the N.A. switch is sent in particular to the engine management control unit and the ABS control unit, VDC function.See E7022 VDC [→939011835]
The control function is activated by the TEG inserted enablement signals (INT) and the command from the switch contact.
The brake light check function monitors that the side lights are operating correctly: the following are checked:
- open circuit (bulb missing or wiring interrupted)
- short-circuit to earth (bulb s.c. or wiring s.c. to earth)
- short circuit to battery voltage (wiring short circuited to Vbatt)
The continuity of the fuse protecting the switch on the brake pedal is also checked.
When one of the situations described above is ascertained, the Body Computer makes the failure status available to the CAN: a special "lights failure" warning light comes on in the instrument panel and, at the same time, the information is shown in the display by means of the specific symbol.
> Note: the central brake light is controlled directly by the switch on the pedal and is not subject to checking.

## E2021 BRAKE LIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939005485]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2021 BRAKE LIGHTS > E2021 BRAKE LIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Station Wagon
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939005485

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The switch I30 receives an ignition-controlled supply (INT) from the fuse line F37 in the junction unit under the dashboard B2: when the brake pedal is pressed, the N.A. switch closes and sends a signal which "passes through" the junction unit under the dashboard B and reaches the Body Computer M1, pin 2 of connector F.
The Body Computer M1 controls the power supply for the brake lights located in the light clusters F30 (left) and F31 (right) from pins 32 and 22 of connector E.
The Body Computer M1 is connected via the CAN line to the instrument panel E50 to manage the lights failure warning light and the brake lights check signal if problems are detected in the circuit or in the fuse.
The switch I30 controls central brake light F40 directly without any control rules, via the junction unit under the dashboard B2, pin 5 of connector D.

## E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS - DESCRIPTION  [939004643]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS > E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Right hand drive
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939004643

#### DESCRIPTION
The vehicle is equipped with a white reversing light located in the left rear light cluster on the moving part of the boot lid.
It is activated each time reverse gear is engaged: this information arrives via the special switch located on the outside of the gearbox casing. The reversing lights circuit is supplied with the TEG inserted (INT) and protected by a special fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard.
The signal that reverse gear has been engaged is managed by the Body Computer which forwards this information to the steering column switch unit for the automatic operation of the rearscreen wiper and, via the CAN, to the other nodes, for example to the parking sensors control unit.
See E3021 REAR WINDOW WASH/WIPE [→939005488]
See E3090 PARKING SENSOR [→939011665]

## E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939004644]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS > E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Right hand drive
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939004644

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The switch for the reversing lights I20 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from the fuse line F35 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2.
When reverse gear is engaged, the switch closes and sends a power supply to the reversing light in the left rear light cluster (moving section) F35, directly via the junction unit B2 from pin 7 of connector D.
The activation signal for the reversing light is also sent to the Body Computer M1 - pin 3 of connector F - and from there to the steering column switch unit H5, for the automatic engagement of the rearscreen wiper.
See E3021 REAR WINDOW WASH/WIPE [→939005488]

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The switch for the reversing lights I20 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from the fuse line F35 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2.
When reverse gear is engaged, the automatic transmission control unit M55 sends the reverse gear engaged signal from pin 13 of connector A to relay T20 in the engine compartment junction unit B1, which sends the power supply to the reversing light in the right rear light cluster, moving section, F36, directly via junction unit B2, from pin 7 of connector D.
The activation signal for the reversing light is also sent to the Body Computer M1 - pin 3 of connector F - and from there to the steering column switch unit H5, for the automatic engagement of the rearscreen wiper.

## E2030 FOG LIGHTS - DESCRIPTION  [939011514]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2030 FOG LIGHTS > E2030 FOG LIGHTS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011514

#### DESCRIPTION
The vehicle is equipped with two additional fog lights, located in the front bumper.
The fog lights are activated via the special button in the controls to the left of the steering wheel; when the lights are on, the warning light in the instrument panel comes on.
A relay located in the engine bay control unit controls fog lamp activation via a line protected by a fuse.
The relay is managed by the Body Computer; the energizing of the relay is activated by:
- the TEG inserted enablement signal (INT);
- a control signal coming from the switch;
- the side lights on signal.
If the side lights are turned off, the fog lamps are deactivated even if the operating button is still pressed. When the side lights are switched on again, the fog lights do not come on automatically, but only when the button is pressed again.
If the TEG is switched off (OFF position) and then switched back on (MAR), the button must be activated again to turn on the fog lights.

## E2030 FOG LIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011515]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2030 FOG LIGHTS > E2030 FOG LIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011515

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The (earth) activation signal for the fog lights reaches pin 1 of connector I of M1 from the control button in the panel to the left of the steering wheel H90.
The side lights activation signal is sent to pin 28 of connector G and 2 of connector I of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unit H5.
See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS [→939002913]
The Body Computer M1 controls the power supply for the fog lights sending an earth signal to the relay T14: of the engine compartment junction unit B1 - from pin 8 of connector A of M1 - which energizes relay T14: this supplies the fog lights F15 (left) and F16 (right). The circuit is protected by fuse F30 of junction unit B2.
The Body Computer M1 is connected via the CAN line to the instrument panel E50 to manage the "fog lights on" warning light.

## E2031 REAR FOG LAMPS - DESCRIPTION  [939004648]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E20 EXTERIOR LIGHTING > E2031 REAR FOG LAMPS > E2031 REAR FOG LAMPS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Right hand drive
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939004648

#### DESCRIPTION
The vehicle is equipped with a red bright rear fog lamp located in the right rear light cluster on the moving part of the boot lid.
The rear fog lamp is activated via the special button in the controls to the left of the steering wheel; when the lights are on, the warning light in the instrument panel comes on.
The switching on of the rear fog lamp is managed by the Body Computer; it is activated by:
- the TEG inserted enablement signal (INT);
- a control signal coming from the switch
- dipped headlamps or fog lights on signal.
If the dipped headlamps lights or the fog lights are turned off, the rear fog lamps are deactivated even if the operating button is still pressed. When the side lights are switched on again, the rear fog lamps do not come on automatically, but only when the button is pressed again.
If the TEG is switched off (OFF position) and then switched back on (MAR), the button must be activated again to turn on the fog lights.
The rear fog lamp check function checks that the light is working properly: the following are checked:
- circuit open or bulb missing
- short-circuit to earth (bulb s.c. or wiring s.c. to earth)
- short circuit to battery voltage (wiring short circuited to Vbatt)
When one of the situations described above is ascertained, the Body Computer makes the failure status available to the CAN: a special "lights failure" warning light comes on in the instrument panel and, at the same time, the information is shown in the display.

## E2510 COURTESY LIGHTS - DESCRIPTION  [939011530]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E25 INTERIOR LIGHTING > E2510 COURTESY LIGHTS > E2510 COURTESY LIGHTS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Low setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011530

#### DESCRIPTION
The front courtesy light includes three lamps with three control switches: it is possible to switch on the corresponding spot light using the outside buttons; the centre button switches the centre light on and off, which is also turned on with a timed delay as described below.
There are two bulbs in the rear courtesy light which can be switched on or off using the relevant button or through a delay timer as described below.
The courtesy light lighting delay is based on a logic managed by the Body Computer whilst the rear courtesy light is operated by the door control unit in accordance with a logic transmitted by the Body Computer via the CAN:
- Pressing the button in the front courtesy light operates both the front courtesy light and the rear courtesy light: in particular, with the courtesy lights off, both are switched on and, with the courtesy lights on, both are switched off.
- When any of the doors is opened both the front and rear courtesy lights come on and there is a timed delay of 3 minutes which is reactivated each time a door is opened.
- When, on the other hand, the button in the front courtesy light is pressed during the timed delay, the courtesy lights are switched off and the timed delay in progress is zeroed.
- When all the doors are closed at the key-off (TEG extrated), the previous timed delay is zeroed and a 10 second timed delay is activated; (this delay is interrupted in the case of a key-on (insertion of the TEG).
- When all the doors are closed at the key-on (insertion of the TEG) the courtesy lights are immediately switched off.
- When the TEG is extracted both the front courtesy light and the rear courtesy light come on and a timed delay of 10 seconds is activated.
- Both the front and rear courtesy lights go out on the "door locking" command.
- Both the front courtesy light and the rear courtesy light come on on the "door unlocking" command and a timed delay of 10 seconds is activated.
- If the inertia switch is operated the courtesy lights come on for 15 minutes.
The switching on or off takes place gradually (dimmer) with the cycle lasting 2 seconds.
If one or more doors are open, this is shown on the instrument panel display; the warning light remain on until all the vehicle doors and boot lid are properly shut. If a given speed limit is exceeded, this is also signalled by means of a buzzer.

## E2510 COURTESY LIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011531]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E25 INTERIOR LIGHTING > E2510 COURTESY LIGHTS > E2510 COURTESY LIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Low setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011531

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The Body Computer M1 receives "door open" input signals at pin 8 (driver's front door) and pin 16 of connector D (left rear door) and at pin 25 (front passenger door) and pin 26 of connector E (right rear door).
Both the front courtesy light G10 and the rear courtesy light G20 receive a power supply from the direct line protected by fuse F39 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2.
The front courtesy light G10 is controlled by the Body Computer M1 : the analogue control signal from the three courtesy light buttons reaches pin 28 of connector E of M1 : the Body Computer M1 consequently supplies the courtesy lights G10, providing a timed earth signal from pins 21, 30 and 37.
The rear courtesy light G20 is controlled by the driver's door control unit M66: the control signal from the buttons on the courtesy light reach pin 12 of connector B, whilst a power supply is sent from pins 13 and 14 to the lights G20.
The Body Computer M1 is connected, via the CAN line, to the instrument panel E50 from which it receives the "inertia switch operated" signal that lights up the courtesy lights and to which a signal that lights up the "doors open" warning light, when necessary, is sent.

The front courtesy light G10 is controlled by the Body Computer M1 : the analogue control signal from the three courtesy light buttons reaches pin 28 of connector E of M1 : the Body Computer M1 consequently supplies the courtesy lights G10, providing a timed earth signal from pins 21, 30 and 37.
The left rear courtesy light G25 is controlled by the front door control unit M66: the control signal from the button on the courtesy light reach pin 12 of connector B, whilst a power supply is sent from pin 14 to the lights G25.
The right rear courtesy light G26 is controlled by the front door control unit M66: the control signal from the button on the courtesy light reach pin 11 of connector B, whilst a power supply is sent from pin 13 to the lights G26.
The Body Computer M1 is connected, via the CAN line, to the instrument panel E50 from which it receives the "inertia switch operated" signal that lights up the courtesy lights and to which a signal that lights up the "doors open" warning light, when necessary, is sent.

## E2510 COURTESY LIGHTS - DESCRIPTION  [939011525]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E25 INTERIOR LIGHTING > E2510 COURTESY LIGHTS > E2510 COURTESY LIGHTS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011525

#### DESCRIPTION
The front courtesy light includes three lamps with three control switches: it is possible to switch on the corresponding spot light using the outside buttons; the centre button switches the centre light on and off, which is also turned on with a timed delay as described below.
There are two bulbs in the rear courtesy light which can be switched on or off using the relevant button or through a delay timer as described below.
The courtesy light lighting delay is based on a logic managed by the Body Computer whilst the rear courtesy light is operated by the door control units in accordance with a logic transmitted by the Body Computer via the CAN:
- Pressing the button in the front courtesy light operates both the front courtesy light and the rear courtesy light: in particular, with the courtesy lights off, both are switched on and, with the courtesy lights on, both are switched off.
- When any of the doors is opened both the front and rear courtesy lights come on and there is a timed delay of 3 minutes which is reactivated each time a door is opened.
- When, on the other hand, the button in the front courtesy light is pressed during the timed delay, the courtesy lights are switched off and the timed delay in progress is zeroed.
- When all the doors are closed at the key-off (TEG extrated), the previous timed delay is zeroed and a 10 second timed delay is activated; (this delay is interrupted in the case of a key-on (insertion of the TEG).
- When all the doors are closed at the key-on (insertion of the TEG) the courtesy lights are immediately switched off.
- When the TEG is extracted both the front courtesy light and the rear courtesy light come on and a timed delay of 10 seconds is activated.
- Both the front and rear courtesy lights go out on the "door locking" command.
- Both the front courtesy light and the rear courtesy light come on on the "door unlocking" command and a timed delay of 10 seconds is activated.
- If the inertia switch is operated the courtesy lights come on for 15 minutes.
The switching on or off takes place gradually (dimmer) with the cycle lasting 2 seconds.
If one or more doors are open, this is shown on the instrument panel display; the warning light remain on until all the vehicle doors and boot lid are properly shut. If a given speed limit is exceeded, this is also signalled by means of a buzzer.

Both the front courtesy light G10 and the rear courtesy light G20 receive a power supply from the direct line protected by fuse F39 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2.
The front courtesy light G10 is controlled by the Body Computer M1 : the analogue control signal from the three courtesy light buttons reaches pin 28 of connector E of M1 : the Body Computer M1 consequently supplies the courtesy lights G10, providing a timed earth signal from pins 21, 30 and 37.
The rear courtesy light G20 is controlled by the driver's door control unit M66 and the passenger door control unit M67: the control signal from the buttons on the courtesy light reach pin 12 of connector B, whilst a power supply is sent from pin 14 to the lights G20.
The Body Computer M1 is connected, via the CAN line, to the instrument panel E50 from which it receives the "inertia switch operated" signal that lights up the courtesy lights and to which a signal that lights up the "doors open" warning light, when necessary, is sent.

## E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - BOOT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT - DESCRIPTION  [939005463]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E25 INTERIOR LIGHTING > E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - LUGGAGE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT > E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - BOOT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Station Wagon
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939005463

#### DESCRIPTION
When the boot is opened the luggage compartment lights come on (two side lights and one central one). They go out when the boot is closed.
The light inside the glove compartment comes on when it is opened and goes out when it is closed.
The lights located beneath each of the sun blinds are turned on by a switch located on the lights themselves.
The Body Computer continuously acquires the battery voltage signal to compare it with a limit figure (SBMT function): if the battery voltage measured is below the level, it intervenes via the CAN sending a signal to disable a series of loads: these include the glove compartment light, the boot light and the sun visor lights; the function is activated after the key-off (TEG extracted).

## E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - BOOT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT - OPERATING DESCRIPTION  [939005464]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E25 INTERIOR LIGHTING > E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - LUGGAGE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT > E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - BOOT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT - OPERATING DESCRIPTION
- Kind: topic
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Station Wagon
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939005464

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
On the basis of the battery voltage control logic (SBMT) described previously, the Body Computer M1 supplies the boot lights G40A, G40B and G41 from pin 23 of connector E. Pin 33 of connector E supplies the driver side sun visor light G31 and passenger side sun visor light G32; pin 16 of connector H supplies the glove compartment light G30 in a similar fashion.
The boot opening switch located in the N47 lock sends an earth signal when the boot is open, which turns the G40A, G40B and G41boot lights on. The same signal is sent to the M1 body computer - pin 36 of connector E, boot open signal; the same signal is used by the alarm system (where fitted).
See E7015 ALARM [→939011825]
the glove compartment light G30 is switched on automatcially - when the switch I30 closes - as the compartment is opened.
The lights in the visors G31 and G32 are switched on by an earth signal sent from the switch on the lights themselves.

## E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - BOOT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT - DESCRIPTION  [939011545]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E25 INTERIOR LIGHTING > E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - LUGGAGE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT > E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - BOOT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011545

#### DESCRIPTION
When the boot is opened the light in the luggage compartment comes on; it goes out when the boot is closed.
The light inside the glove compartment comes on when it is opened and goes out when it is closed.
The lights located beneath each of the sun blinds are turned on by a switch on the lights.
The Body Computer continuously acquires the battery voltage signal to compare it with a limit figure (SBMT function): if the battery voltage measured is below the level, it intervenes via the CAN sending a signal to disable a series of loads: these include the glove compartment light, the boot light and the sun visor lights; the function is activated after the key-off (TEG extracted).

## E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - BOOT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT - OPERATING DESCRIPTION  [939011546]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E25 INTERIOR LIGHTING > E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - LUGGAGE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT > E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - BOOT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT - OPERATING DESCRIPTION
- Kind: topic
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011546

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
On the basis of the battery voltage control logic (SBMT) described previously, the Body Computer M1 supplies the boot light G40 from pin 23 of connector E and the driver's sun visor light G31 and the passenger sun visor light G32 from pin 33 of connector E; the glove compartment light G30 is supplied in a similar manner from pin 16 of connector H.
The boot opening switch is located in the lock N47, it sends an earth signal when the boot is open to light up the relevant courtesy light G40; the same signal is sent to the Body Computer M1 - pin 36 of connector E "boot open" signal; the same signal is used by the alarm system, when fitted.
See E7015 ALARM [→939011825]
the glove compartment light G30 is switched on automatcially - when the switch I30 closes - as the compartment is opened.
The lights in the visors G31 and G32 are switched on by an earth signal sent from the switch on the lights themselves.

## E2521 PUDDLE LIGHTS - DESCRIPTION  [939011555]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E25 INTERIOR LIGHTING > E2521 COURTESY LIGHTS > E2521 PUDDLE LIGHTS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Low setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011555

#### DESCRIPTION
There are two lights for lighting up the ground ("puddle lights") in the front front doors.
The driver's front door control unit detects the door status, notifies the Body Computer and controls the switching on of the light in the two doors.
The opening of one of the front doors causes the two lights to come on for a maximum of 3 minutes; when this time has expired the light can only be switched back on again after the door has been reopened.
The closing of the driver's door causes the two lights to go out immediately.

## E2521 PUDDLE LIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011556]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E25 INTERIOR LIGHTING > E2521 COURTESY LIGHTS > E2521 PUDDLE LIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Low setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011556

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The Body Computer M1 receives door open input signals at pin 8 of connector D (driver's front door) and 25 of connector E (passenger side door).
The puddle lights G51 and G52 are operated by the driver's door control lunit M66.
The control unit M66 receives a power supply - at pin 11 of connector D - from the line protected by fuse F36 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2; on the basis of the logic described previously, the control unit M66 supplies the relevant puddle light G51, from pins 17 and 18 of connector B and the passenger puddle light G52 from pin 21 of connector B.

- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E25 INTERIOR LIGHTING > E2521 COURTESY LIGHTS > E2521 PUDDLE LIGHTS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011550

#### DESCRIPTION
There are two lights for lighting up the ground ("puddle lights") in the front front doors.
The two door control units detect the status of the doors, notify the Body Computer and directly control the switching on of the bulb in the door.
The opening of one of the front doors causes the relevant light to come on for a maximum of 3 minutes; when this time has expired the light can only be switched back on again after the door has been reopened.
The closing of the driver's door causes the two lights to go out immediately.

## E2521 PUDDLE LIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011551]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E25 INTERIOR LIGHTING > E2521 COURTESY LIGHTS > E2521 PUDDLE LIGHTS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)

- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011551

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The Body Computer M1 receives door open input signals at pin 8 of connector D (driver's front door) and 25 of connector E (passenger side door).
The puddle lights G51 and G52 are operated by the driver's door control unit M66 and the passenger door control unit M67 connected by the CAN line to the Body Computer M1.
The control units M66 and M67 receive a power supply - at pin 11 of connector D - from the line protected by fuse F32 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2; on the basis of the logic described previously, each control unit supplies the relevant puddle light G51 and G52, from pins 17 and 18 of connector B.
