## E2535 LIGHTING CONTROLS - DESCRIPTION  [939011565]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E25 INTERIOR LIGHTING > E2535 CONTROL LIGHTS > E2535 LIGHTING CONTROLS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Low setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011565

#### DESCRIPTION
The car is equipped with numerous light sources for optimal lighting of interior instruments and controls.
Some of these are lit with the ignition ON (INT), others with the side lights on, others are dimmable in accordance with a rheostat-controlled adjustment strategy managed by the Body Computer.
The Body Computer manages the lighting - with the side lights on - of:
- cigar lighter and rear current socket;
- controls on the front courtesy light
- radio display (aftermarket version only)
See E3510 RADIO [→939003053]
- radio phone preparation
See E3580 PREPARATION FOR CELLULAR TELEPHONE [→939011706]
The Body Computer manages (directly and via the door control units) the dimmed lighting of:
- instrument panel and display;
- auxiliary instrument
- switches in the doors;
- climate control system controls.
All the other controls are lit up when the ignition is on (INT), i.e. with the TEG inserted.
A brightness sensor for the automatic adjustment (day/night) of the brightness of the instrument panel is built-in; it has the task of measuring the ambient light conditions and sending this information (daytime or nightime) to the Body Computer which, on comparing this information with the state of the side lights, selects the appropriate lighting configuration for the vehicle interior (daytime or nightime mode).
With this information available, the behaviour of the instrument is as follows:
- In "daytime" mode the display can be adjusted to 8 settings, the graphics are switched off, the index lighting is 100% and cannot be adjusted.
- In "nightime" mode the display, the graphics and the indexes can be adjusted to 8 settings and the level set will be transmitted to the components that regulate the brightness (climate control display, radio display).
This adjustment is made using the "MODE", "MODE +" and "MODE -" buttons located on the steering column switch unit; there are 8 different possible settings. (fom 30% to 100% of the maximum intensity). The level set by pressing the buttons is shown on the instrument panel display; the setting is also memorized and used later on.

## E2535 LIGHTING CONTROLS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011566]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E25 INTERIOR LIGHTING > E2535 CONTROL LIGHTS > E2535 LIGHTING CONTROLS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Low setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011566

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The "MODE" "+" and "-" controls, located on the left steering column switch unit lever +15, send an analogue signal to the instrument panel E50 at pin 5 of connector A.
The dimmed power supply for the auxiliary instruments E20 leaves pin 5 of connector C of E50 (pin 2 of connector C provides the reference earth).
The Body Computer M1 is connected via the CAN line to the instrument panel E50 from which it receives the "brightness adjustment" signal which is transmitted to the radio node and to the climate control system control unit
See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES [→939011452]
The power supply with the side lights switched on is provided by the Body Computer M1 - pin 40 of connector E for the cigar lighter light P50 and the rear current socket P51, in addition to the controls on the front courtesy light G10; the same lighting is sent, - pin 18 of connector H of M1 - to the controls for the radio P20 and to the preparation for the radio telephone D75.
The lighting for the front door controls H44 and H50 is managed by the door control units M66 - at pin 11 of of connector D by the line protected by fuse F32 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2 , and connected via the CAN line to the Body Computer M1 .
The ignition-controlled power supply line (INT), protected by fuse F35 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2, provides the lighting for the switch unit on the tunnel H35.
The ignition-operated power supply line (INT), protected by fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2, provides the lighting for the hazard warning lights control H20, the control panel to the left of the dashboard H90, the controls on the rear courtesy light G20, those on the seats I65 and I66 and the passenger side front door electric window switch H50.

#### DESCRIPTION
The car is equipped with numerous light sources for optimal lighting of interior instruments and controls.
Some of these are lit with the ignition ON (INT), others with the side lights on, others are dimmable in accordance with a rheostat-controlled adjustment strategy managed by the Body Computer.
The Body Computer manages the lighting - with the side lights on - of:
- cigar lighter and rear current socket;
- controls on the front courtesy light
The Body Computer manages (directly and via the door and boot node control units) the dimmed lighting of:
- instrument panel and display;
- auxiliary instrument
- switches in the doors;
- climate control system controls;
- built-in radio-telephone-navigator unit;
All the other controls are lit up when the ignition is on (INT), i.e. with the TEG inserted.
A brightness sensor for the automatic adjustment (day/night) of the brightness of the instrument panel is built-in; it has the task of measuring the ambient light conditions and sending this information (daytime or nightime) to the Body Computer which, on comparing this information with the state of the side lights, selects the appropriate lighting configuration for the vehicle interior (daytime or nightime mode).
With this information available, the behaviour of the instrument is as follows:
- In "daytime" mode the display can be adjusted to 8 settings, the graphics are switched off, the index lighting is 100% and cannot be adjusted.
- In "nightime" mode the display, the graphics and the indexes can be adjusted to 8 settings and the level set will be transmitted to the components that regulate the brightness (climate control display, radio display).
This adjustment is made using the "MODE", "MODE +" and "MODE -" buttons located on the steering column switch unit; there are 8 different possible settings. (fom 30% to 100% of the maximum intensity). The level set by pressing the buttons is shown on the instrument panel display; the setting is also memorized and used later on.

## E2535 LIGHTING CONTROLS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011561]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E25 INTERIOR LIGHTING > E2535 CONTROL LIGHTS > E2535 LIGHTING CONTROLS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011561

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The "MODE" "+" and "-" controls, located on the left steering column switch unit lever +15, send an analogue signal to the instrument panel E50 at pin 5 of connector A.
The dimmed power supply for the auxiliary instruments E20 leaves pin 5 of connector C of E50 (pin 2 of connector C provides the reference earth).
The Body Computer M1 is connected via the CAN line to the instrument panel E50 from which it receives the "brightness adjustment" signal which is transmitted to the radio node and to the climate control system control unit
See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES [→939011452]
The power supply with the side lights on is sent from the Body Computer M1 - pin 40 of connector E to the cigar lighter light P50 and the rear current socket P51 as well as to the controls on the front courtesy light G10.
The lighting of the front door controls H44 and H50 is managed by the driver side door control unit M66 and passenger side door control unit M67 , supplied at pin 11 of connector D by a line protected by fuse F32 of the underfacia control unit B2 , and connected via the CAN line to the Body Computer M1 .
Similarly, the lighting of the rear door controls H53 and H54 is managed by the boot control unit M63 , supplied - at pin B8 of connector A - by a line protected by fuse F36 of the underfacia control unit B2 , and connected via the CAN line to the Body Computer M1 .
The ignition-controlled power supply line (INT), protected by fuse F35 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2, provides the lighting for the switch unit on the tunnel H35.
The ignition-operated power supply line (INT), protected by fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2, provides the lighting for the hazard warning lights control H20, the control panel to the left of the dashboard H90, the radio controls on the steering wheel D47, the controls on the rear courtesy light G20 and those on the seats I65 and I66.

## E3010 HORNS - DESCRIPTION  [939011571]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3010 HORNS > E3010 HORNS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011571

#### DESCRIPTION
The vehicle is equipped with a horn system consisting of two horns with different tones: one high tone and one low tone: the two horns come on simultaneously.
The horns are operated by pressing the sides of the steering wheel cover (around the Air Bag).
The horn circuit is protected by a specific fuse and controlled by a relay located in the engine compartment junction unit.
For safety reasons, the horns can be operated at any time even with the TEG switched off.

## E3010 HORNS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011572]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3010 HORNS > E3010 HORNS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011572

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The system for the horns receives a power supply via the horn relay T3 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 from the line directly from the battery via fuse F10 in junction unit B1.
The relay coil is energized by an earth signal produced by the closing of one of the switches on the steering wheel, connected via the wiring through the clock spring D47. The relay thereby supplies the horns P05.

## E3020 WINDSCREEN WASH/WIPE - DESCRIPTION  [939011576]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3020 WINDSCREEN WASH/WIPE > E3020 WINDSCREEN WASH/WIPE - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011576

#### DESCRIPTION
The windscreen wash/wipe system is activated by the lever located on the right of the steering wheel, with the following functions: there are five possible positions for the lever, turning it upwards, corresponding to:
- windscreen wiper off (stationary);
- intermittent/automatic operation;
- continuous slow operation;
- continuous fast operation;
- "antipanic" temporary fast operation (unstable position, turning the lever downwards).
In the intermittent/automatic operation position three different positions can be selected by turning the ring nut:
- on the "LOW" version the different intermittent speeds are switched on (from the slowest to the fastest;
- on the "HIGH" version with the rain sensor: the different sensor settings are switched on: the activation of the rain sensor involves a windscreen wiper arm stroke as feedback to confirm that it has been switched on.
The frequency of the windscreen wiper strokes is automatically adjusted depending on the amount of water on the windscreen detected by the sensor: the frequency varies continuously from nil (no stroke - windscreen dry) to wiping at the second continuous speed (heavy rain).
The windscreen washer function can be activated by pulling the lever toward the steering wheel: this activates the windscreen washer pump: keeping the lever pulled also switched on the windscreen wiper in accordance with a specific control logic: the windscreen wiper is activated at the first speed: when the windscreen washer control is no longer present, an additional stroke is carried out.
The screen washer fluid reservoir has a sensor that signals a decrease in the level by means of a special warning light in the instrument panel.
The windscreen wash/wipe circuit is protected by a specific fuse and controlled by the ignition-operated exclusion relay (INT/A) located in the junction unit under the dashboard. The windscreen wiper and the windscreen washer can be activated with the TEG inserted and after starting (INT/A).
The correct operation of the rain sensor is controlled by the check function. If the rain sensor is not working properly, the windscreen wiper will operate intermittently whilst the instrument panel display will show the sensor failure.

## E3020 WINDSCREEN WASH/WIPE - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011577]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3020 WINDSCREEN WASH/WIPE > E3020 WINDSCREEN WASH/WIPE - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011577

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The electronic device inside the steering column switch unit H5 and the controls on the right lever receive a power supply at pin 11 of connector A from the ignition-controlled line (INT/A) of relay T12 protected by fuse F43, both housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B2.
Pin 7 of connector A and 9 of connector C of H5 are earthed.
According to the function selected, stalk unit H5 (connector A) sends the following control signals to the wiper motor N15:
- from pin 8 for fast operation;
- from pin 9 for slow and/or intermittent operation,
- pin 6, on the other hand, receives the earth signal coming from the motor end of travel cam which stops operation. The windscreen wiper motor N15 is then earthed.
The rain sensor housed in the mirror P65 receives a supply from the INT line protected by fuse F49 of the junction unit B2 and sends the automatic operating signal to pin 2 of connector A of H5 via the A-BUS serial line of the Body Computer M1 pin 7 of connector D and pin 25 of connector B.
The Body Computer M1 is connected via the CAN line to the instrument panel E50 to manage the failure signal if there are problems with the rain sensor.
The screen washer fluid level sensor k27 sends an earth signal to the instrument panel E50 - pin 12 of connector D - which lights up the warning light directly.

## E3021 REARSCREEN WASH/WIPE - DESCRIPTION  [939005489]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3021 REAR WINDOW WASH/WIPE > E3021 REARSCREEN WASH/WIPE - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Station Wagon
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939005489

#### DESCRIPTION
The rear wiper control is activated by turning the three-position wheel anticlockwise:
- stable central position, equivalent to OFF;
- 2 unstable positions: rear wiper activation and rear washer activation.
The rear wiper is controlled by the stalk intermittently with an interval of 5 seconds between the end of one stroke and the beginning of the next.
The motor is activated throughout the duration of the command and until the brush is reparked.
> Note: With the windscreen wipers working, if reverse gear is engaged, the rearscreen wiper is automatically activated: this function is managed by the Body Computer, which receives information from the reversing switchSee E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS - DESCRIPTION [→939004643]
Pushing the right steering column switch unit lever activates the rear washing. Keeping the lever pushed for more than 0.5 secs automatically activates the rearscreen wiper at the continuous speed.
The windscreen wash/wipe circuit is protected by a specific fuse and controlled by the ignition-operated exclusion relay (INT/A) located in the junction unit under the dashboard. The windscreen wiper and the windscreen washer can be activated with the TEG inserted and after starting (INT/A).

## E3021 REARSCREEN WASH/WIPE - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939005490]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3021 REAR WINDOW WASH/WIPE > E3021 REARSCREEN WASH/WIPE - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Station Wagon
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939005490

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The electronic device inside the steering column switch unit H5 and the controls on the right lever receive a power supply at pin 11 of connector A from the ignition-controlled line (INT/A) of relay T12 protected by fuse F43, both housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B2.
Pin 7 of connector A and 9 of connector C of H5 are earthed.
The electronic device inside the steering column switch unit H5, which controls the rear wiper receive a power supply at pin 12 of connector C from the ignition-controlled line (INT/A) of relay T12 protected by fuse F52, both housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B2.
Steering wheel stalk unit H5 sends a command to rear wiper motor N16 from pin 1 of connector B while pin 2 receives an earth signal from the motor end stop cam, which stops operation.
Pin 3 of connector A of H5 receives the reverse engaged signal for automatic rear wiper operation.
The steering column switch unit H5 windscreen washer switch, once activated, sends two signals from pins 10 and 12 of connector A which operate the windscreen washer pump N22 which turns sending the washer fluid to the windscreen wiper.

## E3022 HEADLAMP WASHER - DESCRIPTION  [939011581]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3022 HEADLAMP WASHER > E3022 HEADLAMP WASHER - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011581

#### DESCRIPTION
The headlamp washer cleans the headlamp lenses as the windscreen is being cleaned.
The headlamp washer function is managed by the Body Computer which automatically activates the headlamp washer, with the dipped headlamps on, when the windscreen washers are activated through the lever on the right of the steering wheel.
The headlamp washer consists of a pump that sends detergent to two nozzles located in the bumpers which spray a powerful jet onto the headlamps.
A timer activates the headlamp washer pump by means of a series of pulses lasting about half a second.
The headlamp washer circuit is protected by a fuse and governed by a special relay located in the engine compartment junction unit.

## E3022 HEADLAMP WASHER - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011582]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3022 HEADLAMP WASHER > E3022 HEADLAMP WASHER - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011582

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The relay T17 in the engine compartment junction unit B1 receives a power supply from the line for fuse F9, from the engine compartment junction unit B1, whilst the energizing takes place through the ignition-operated line (INT/A) from fuse F31 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2.
The relay operates the headlamp washer pump N25 directly when an earth signal arrives from the Body Computer M1; this signal - from pin 14 of connector A - is sent on the basis of the positive windscreen washer request signal coming from the steering column switch unit H5 - pin 5 of connector A and in the presence of the dipped headlamps on enablement (pin 2 of connector I and pin 28 of connector G of M1).
See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS [→939002923]

## E3030 DEMISTING REARSCREEN AND REAR VIEW MIRRORS - DESCRIPTION  [939004653]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3030 HEATED REAR WINDSCREEN AND DOOR MIRROR DEFROSTING > E3030 DEMISTING REARSCREEN AND REAR VIEW MIRRORS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; period: From 01/06; only with equipment: High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939004653

#### DESCRIPTION
In the case of poor visibility it is possible to activate the demisting of the rearscreen, the exterior rear view mirrors and the lower part of the windscreen.
The heating resistances for these components absorb a considerable amount of energy and are therefore controlled and, possibly, deactivated after they have been working for a certain length of time: the demisting is subject to a delay timer, managed by the Body Computer, according to the following logic:
- TEG inserted, starting excluded (INT/A);
- engagement signal coming from the special button in the climate control system control panel.
Under these circumstances the resistances remain supplied for a maximum of 20 minutes, then the supply is cut off.
The supply is cut off in the following conditions:
- TEG extracted (key-off);
- disengagement signal from the button;
- battery voltage below 8.5 V;
- after the first 15 minutes of operation if the engine speed is below 960 rpm.
With the defrosting on the warning light in the climate control system controls also comes on.
The activation timer (20 minutes) is set again each time the button is operated.
The climate control system control unit logic also intervenes with the "MAX-DEF" command in accordance with the logic described previously.
The "MAX-DEF" function lasts for 3 minutes starting from when the engine temperature exceeds a certain limit.
> Note: the deactivation of the MAX-DEF control only causes the switching off of the heated rear windscreen if the command to switch it on came from the MAX-DEF button; if, on the other hand, the command was given via the heated rear windscreen button, it remains on)
The rearscreen defrosting circuit is controlled by the heated rear windscreen relay and protected by a specific fuse, located in the junction unit under the dashboard. This circuit is controlled by the logic described above directly by the Body Computer.
The defrosting circuit for the door mirrors, on the other hand, is protected by another fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard and is controlled by the door control units, in accordance with the logic transmitted by the Body Computer via the CAN.
The windscreen defrosting circuit is operated by a special relay located in the engine compartment junction unit and protected by a specific fuse also in that junction unit.

## E3030 DEMISTING REARSCREEN AND REAR VIEW MIRRORS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939004654]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3030 HEATED REAR WINDSCREEN AND DOOR MIRROR DEFROSTING > E3030 DEMISTING REARSCREEN AND REAR VIEW MIRRORS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; period: From 01/06; only with equipment: High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939004654

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The heated rear windscreen relay T11, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B2, controls the engagement of the heated rear windscreen P55 defrosting resistances via the line protected by fuse F40 of junction unit B2.
Similarly, the engagement of the defrosting resistances for the windscreen P56 are operated via the line protected by fuse F41 of junction unit B2 and relay T19 and fuse F20 located in the engine compartment junction unit B1.
The coil for relay T11 receives an ignition-operated power supply (INT/A) and is energized by an earth signal coming from the Body Computer M1 - pin 6 of connector F; this signal is sent on the basis of the previously illustrated control logic and in the presence of the heated rear windscreen engagement command or through the MAX-DEF function coming via the CAN from the climate control system control unit M70.
The engagement of the defrosting resistances for the door mirrors P60 and P61 is controlled by the control units for the driver's door M66 and passenger door M67 connected via the CAN line to the Body Computer M1.
Control units M66 and M67 receive a supply - at pin 11 of connector D - from the line protected by fuse F32 of underfacia control unit B2 .
On the basis of the complex control logic illustrated previously, the engagement command for the defrosting is sent via the CAN to the two door control units as well which control the resistances located in mirrors P60 and P61 from pins 7 and 9 of connector E of M66 and M67.

## E3030 DEMISTING REARSCREEN AND REAR VIEW MIRRORS - DESCRIPTION  [939011586]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3030 HEATED REAR WINDSCREEN AND DOOR MIRROR DEFROSTING > E3030 DEMISTING REARSCREEN AND REAR VIEW MIRRORS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; period: Up to 12/05; only with equipment: High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011586

#### DESCRIPTION
In the case of poor visibility it is possible to activate the demisting of the rearscreen, the exterior rear view mirrors and the lower part of the windscreen.
The heating resistances for these components absorb a considerable amount of energy and are therefore controlled and, possibly, deactivated after they have been working for a certain length of time: the demisting is subject to a delay timer, managed by the Body Computer, according to the following logic:
- TEG inserted, starting excluded (INT/A);
- engagement signal coming from the special button in the climate control system control panel.
Under these circumstances the resistances remain supplied for a maximum of 20 minutes, then the supply is cut off.
The supply is cut off in the following conditions:
- TEG extracted (key-off);
- disengagement signal from the button;
- battery voltage below 8.5 V;
- after the first 15 minutes of operation if the engine speed is below 960 rpm.
With the defrosting on the warning light in the climate control system controls also comes on.
The activation timer (20 minutes) is set again each time the button is operated.
The climate control system control unit logic also intervenes with the "MAX-DEF" command in accordance with the logic described previously.
The "MAX-DEF" function lasts for 3 minutes starting from when the engine temperature exceeds a certain limit.
> Note: the deactivation of the MAX-DEF control only causes the switching off of the heated rear windscreen if the command to switch it on came from the MAX-DEF button; if, on the other hand, the command was given via the heated rear windscreen button, it remains on)
The rearscreen defrosting circuit is controlled by the heated rear windscreen relay and protected by a specific fuse, located in the junction unit under the dashboard. This circuit is controlled by the logic described above directly by the Body Computer.
The defrosting circuit for the door mirrors, on the other hand, is protected by another fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard and is controlled by the door control units, in accordance with the logic transmitted by the Body Computer via the CAN.
The windscreen defrosting circuit is operated by a special relay located in the boot junction unit and protected by a specific fuse also in that junction unit.

## E3030 DEMISTING REARSCREEN AND REAR VIEW MIRRORS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011587]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3030 HEATED REAR WINDSCREEN AND DOOR MIRROR DEFROSTING > E3030 DEMISTING REARSCREEN AND REAR VIEW MIRRORS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; period: Up to 12/05; only with equipment: High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011587

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The heated rear windscreen relay T11, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B2, controls the engagement of the heated rear windscreen P55 defrosting resistances via the line protected by fuse F40 of junction unit B2.
Similarly, the engagement of the defrosting resistances for the windscreen P56 are operated via the line protected by fuse F41 of junction unit B2 and relay T22 and fuse F59 located in the boot junction unit B45.
The coil for relay T11 receives an ignition-operated power supply (INT/A) and is energized by an earth signal coming from the Body Computer M1 - pin 6 of connector F; this signal is sent on the basis of the previously illustrated control logic and in the presence of the heated rear windscreen engagement command or through the MAX-DEF function coming via the CAN from the climate control system control unit M70.
The engagement of the defrosting resistances for the door mirrors P60 and P61 is controlled by the control units for the driver's door M66 and passenger door M67 connected via the CAN line to the Body Computer M1.
Control units M66 and M67 receive a supply - at pin 11 of connector D - from the line protected by fuse F32 of underfacia control unit B2 .
On the basis of the complex control logic illustrated previously, the engagement command for the defrosting is sent via the CAN to the two door control units as well which control the resistances located in mirrors P60 and P61 from pins 7 and 9 of connector E of M66 and M67.

> Note: the deactivation of the MAX-DEF control only causes the switching off of the heated rear windscreen if the command to switch it on came from the MAX-DEF button; if, on the other hand, the command was given via the heated rear windscreen button, it remains on)
The rearscreen defrosting circuit is controlled by the heated rear windscreen relay and protected by a specific fuse, located in the junction unit under the dashboard. This circuit is controlled by the logic described above directly by the Body Computer.
The defrosting circuit for the door mirrors, on the other hand, is protected by another fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard and is controlled by the door control units, in accordance with the logic transmitted by the Body Computer via the CAN.
The windscreen defrosting circuit is operated by a special relay located in the engine compartment junction unit and protected by a specific fuse also in that junction unit.

## E3030 DEMISTING REARSCREEN AND REAR VIEW MIRRORS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939005501]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3030 HEATED REAR WINDSCREEN AND DOOR MIRROR DEFROSTING > E3030 DEMISTING REARSCREEN AND REAR VIEW MIRRORS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Station Wagon, High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939005501

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The heated rear windscreen relay T11, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B2, controls the engagement of the heated rear windscreen P55 defrosting resistances via the line protected by fuse F40 of junction unit B2.
Similarly, the engagement of the defrosting resistances for the windscreen P56 are operated via the line protected by fuse F41 of junction unit B2 and relay T19 and fuse F20 located in the engine compartment junction unit B1.
The coil for relay T11 receives an ignition-operated power supply (INT/A) and is energized by an earth signal coming from the Body Computer M1 - pin 6 of connector F; this signal is sent on the basis of the previously illustrated control logic and in the presence of the heated rear windscreen engagement command or through the MAX-DEF function coming via the CAN from the climate control system control unit M70.
The engagement of the defrosting resistances for the door mirrors P60 and P61 is controlled by the control units for the driver's door M66 and passenger door M67 connected via the CAN line to the Body Computer M1.
Control units M66 and M67 receive a supply - at pin 11 of connector D - from the line protected by fuse F32 of underfacia control unit B2 .
On the basis of the complex control logic illustrated previously, the engagement command for the defrosting is sent via the CAN to the two door control units as well which control the resistances located in mirrors P60 and P61 from pins 7 and 9 of connector E of M66 and M67.

## E3030 DEMISTING REARSCREEN AND REAR VIEW MIRRORS - DESCRIPTION  [939011591]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3030 HEATED REAR WINDSCREEN AND DOOR MIRROR DEFROSTING > E3030 DEMISTING REARSCREEN AND REAR VIEW MIRRORS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Low setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011591

#### DESCRIPTION
In the case of poor visibility it is possible to activate the demisting of the rearscreen and the exterior rear view mirrors.
The heating resistances for these components absorb a considerable amount of energy and are therefore controlled and, possibly, deactivated after they have been working for a certain length of time: the demisting is subject to a delay timer, managed by the Body Computer, according to the following logic:
- TEG inserted, starting excluded (INT/A);
- engagement signal coming from the special button in the climate control system control panel.
Under these circumstances the resistances remain supplied for a maximum of 20 minutes, then the supply is cut off.
The supply is cut off in the following conditions:
- TEG extracted (key-off);
- disengagement signal from the button;
- battery voltage below 8.5 V;
- after the first 15 minutes of operation if the engine speed is below 960 rpm.
With the defrosting on the warning light in the climate control system controls also comes on.
The activation timer (20 minutes) is set again each time the button is operated.
The climate control system control unit logic also intervenes with the "MAX-DEF" command in accordance with the logic described previously.
The "MAX-DEF" function lasts for 3 minutes starting from when the engine temperature exceeds a certain limit.
> Note: the deactivation of the MAX-DEF control only causes the switching off of the heated rear windscreen if the command to switch it on came from the MAX-DEF button; if, on the other hand, the command was given via the heated rear windscreen button, it remains on)
The rearscreen defrosting circuit is controlled by the heated rear windscreen relay and protected by a specific fuse, located in the junction unit under the dashboard. This circuit is controlled by the logic described above directly by the Body Computer.
The defrosting circuit for the door mirrors, on the other hand, is protected by another fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard and is controlled by the door control units, in accordance with the logic transmitted by the Body Computer via the CAN.

- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Low setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011592

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The heated rear windscreen relay T11, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B2, controls the engagement of the heated rear windscreen P55 defrosting resistances via the line protected by fuse F40 of junction unit B2.
The coil for relay T11 receives an ignition-operated power supply (INT/A) and is energized by an earth signal coming from the Body Computer M1 - pin 6 of connector F; this signal is sent on the basis of the previously illustrated control logic and in the presence of the heated rear windscreen engagement command or through the MAX-DEF function coming via the CAN from the climate control system control unit M70.
The engagement of the defrosting resistances for the door mirrors P60 and P61 is controlled by the control units for the driver's door M66 and the passenger door M67.
Control units M66 and M67 receive a supply - at pin 5 of connector C and 11 of connector A - from the line protected by fuse F41 of junction unit under the dashboard B2 .

## E3032 REAR VIEW MIRROR ADJUSTMENT - DESCRIPTION  [939011601]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3032 DOOR MIRROR ADJUSTMENT > E3032 REAR VIEW MIRROR ADJUSTMENT - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Low setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011601

#### DESCRIPTION
The door mirrors can be electrically adjusted in two directions using a joystick control located in the door controls on the driver's side: a selection cursor makes it possible to choose either the left or the right mirror. The button controls two electrical motors located in each of the two mirrors: one motor allows the rotation of the mirror on the horizontal axis, another on the vertical axis.
The circuit is protected by a fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard and is operated by the door control unit in accordance with the control logic transmitted by the Body Computer via the CAN.

## E3032 REAR VIEW MIRROR ADJUSTMENT - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011602]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3032 DOOR MIRROR ADJUSTMENT > E3032 REAR VIEW MIRROR ADJUSTMENT - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Low setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011602

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
Control unit M66 is supplied at pin 11 of connector D - by a line protected by fuse F36 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2 .
The controls on the driver's door H44 include the joystick and control switch for the exterior rear view mirrors:
- selection of the right/left mirror: signal to pin 30 of connector A of M66,
- vertical movement: signal to pin 28 of connector A of M66,
- horizontal movement: signal to pin 29 of connector A of M66.
On the basis of the commands received, the control unit M66 controls the motor for the mirrors P60 from pin 4 of connector E (joint) and for pins 3 and 5 (horizontal and vertical movement respectively).
Similarly, the same commands are sent to the passenger side mirror P61 from pins 10, 26 and 27 of connector B of M66.

## E3032 REAR VIEW MIRROR ADJUSTMENT - DESCRIPTION  [939011596]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3032 DOOR MIRROR ADJUSTMENT > E3032 REAR VIEW MIRROR ADJUSTMENT - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011596

#### DESCRIPTION
The door mirrors can be electrically adjusted in two directions using a joystick control located in the door controls on the driver's side: a selection cursor makes it possible to choose either the left or the right mirror. The button controls two electrical motors located in each of the two mirrors: one motor allows the rotation of the mirror on the horizontal axis, another on the vertical axis.
Another button controls the folding back of the mirrors if required (for example when trying to get through a narrow space).
On the HIGH version, in addition to moving the door mirrors manually, it is possible to memorize and later on recall 3 positions defined in relation to the position of the driver's seat; the passenger side rear view mirror is also positioned automatically when reverse gear is engaged.
This entire complex logic is managed by the driver's seat control unit which converses with the Body Computer via the CAN
See E3076 ELECTRICALLY-ADJUSTABLE SEATS [→939011650]
The interior rear view mirror is electrochrome type: i.e. it contains an electronic device which controls the automatic anti-glare function. The automatic antiglare function is disabled when reverse is engaged.
The circuit is protected by a fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard and is operated by the door control units in accordance with the control logic transmitted by the Body Computer via the CAN.
The interior rear view mirror power supply circuit is protected by a fuse in the under-dashboard control unit.

## E3032 REAR VIEW MIRROR ADJUSTMENT - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011597]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3032 DOOR MIRROR ADJUSTMENT > E3032 REAR VIEW MIRROR ADJUSTMENT - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011597

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The motors for the exterior rear view mirrors in P60 and P61 are operated by the driver's door control unit M66 and the passenger door control unit M67, connected to one another via the CAN line and to the Body Computer M1 and to the driver's seat movement and memory control unit H66.
See E3076 ELECTRICALLY-ADJUSTABLE SEATS [→939011650]
The two mirrors contain a potentiometer for each motor which detects the position and sends a feedback signal to the control unit to pins 10 and 11 of connector E of M66 and M67. (pins 15 and 17 of connector E provide a power supply and earth for the potentiometers).
Control units M66 and M67 receive a supply - at pin 11 of connector D - from the line protected by fuse F32 of underfacia control unit B2 .
The controls on the driver's door H44 include the joystick and control switch for the exterior rear view mirrors:
- selection of the right/left mirror: signal to pin 30 of connector A of M66,
- vertical movement: signal to pin 28 of connector A of M66,
- horizontal movement: signal to pin 29 of connector A of M66,
- mirror folding: signal to pin 20 of connector B of M66.
On the basis of the requests set whilst driving or on the basis of values memorized, the control units M66 and M67 control the motors for mirrors P60 and P61 from pin 4 of connector E (joint) and pins 3 and 5 (horizontal and vertical movement respectively).
The folding motors are controlled from pins 1 and 8 of connector E of M66 and M67.
Electrochrome mirror P65 supplies an ignition-controlled power supply (INT) - from pin 23 of connector D - from a line protected by fuse F32 of under-dashboard control unit B2.
The switch for the reversing lights I20 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from the fuse line F35 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2.
When reverse is engaged, the switch closes to send a control signal to mirror P65 through control unit B2 - from pin 8 of connector D.

## E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING - DESCRIPTION  [939011611]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING > E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Low setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011611

#### DESCRIPTION
The simultaneous operation of the four door locks takes place via:
- TEG the remote control;
- the locking/unlocking button in the centre console.
The TEG remote has 3 buttons which allow the operation of the central locking system: a button for unlocking the doors, one for locking the vehicle and one for releasing the boot
See descriptions 5520 ENGINE STARTING [→939003530 5520 ENGINE STARTING]
The door unlocking/locking management strategy is carried out by the door control unit which controls the effective state of the locks through the signals arriving from the switches in the actual locks and the emergency key pawl (driver's door only) in this way the "locking" command is only carried out with all the doors properly shut and the locks unlocked; conversely, the "unlocking" command is only carried out with the locks locked.
The locks have an additional motor that carries out the dead lock function which allows the interior door opening handles to be mechanically disconnected so that it is no longer possible to open the door from the inside (for example, after having broken the glass in a theft attempt); the dead lock function also inhibits the operation of the door locking/unlocking buttons in the dashboard.
The dead lock function is switched on at the time the doors are locked or by pressing the remote control twice.
An LED next to the two above mentioned controls makes the following signals:
- locking of the locks: the LED lights up for 3 seconds. If some of the doors or the boot are not properly shut at the time when the locks are locked, the LED flashes at 3 Hz for 3 seconds;
- dead lock activation: the LED flashes twice for 0.5 seconds;
- unlocking the locks: the LED goes out.
The instrument panel acquires the door status signal via the CAN and lights up the "doors open" warning light and, at the same time, the information is shown on the display; in addition, if one of the doors or the boot or the bonnet is open and the speed of the vehicle exceeds around 4 km/h, an acoustic warning is also emitted.
It is possible, using the special setup in the instrument panel, to select whether to unlock all the doors or only the driver's front door, whilst all the other doors and the boot remain locked.
It is possible to enable/disable the locking of the doors above a certain speed threshold (20 km/h) using the special setup in the instrument panel: in this case the Body Computer implements the locking of the doors when this threshold is exceeded. When the speed returns below this level, the doors and the boot remain locked; later on, when one of the doors is opened, the function is re-enabled and, if the threshold is exceeded, the doors are locked once again.
The boot unlocking operating mode can be selected still using the special setup in the instrument panel:
- assisted boot unlocking: the tailgate is considered as a fifth door to all intents and purposes;
- independent boot unlocking: the boot is locked when the doors are locked, whilst it can be unlocked independently of the unlocking of the doors.
See E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING - DESCRIPTION [→939005505]
The doors are automatically unlocked if the inertia switch is operated: the instrument panel receives a signal from the switch, lights up the appropriate warning light and notifies the Body Computer via the CAN.
The central locking circuit is protected by a specific fuse located in the junction unit under the dashboard.

## E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011612]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING > E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Low setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011612

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The locking/unlocking function for the doors is operated by the front doors control unit M66 connected via the CAN line to the Body Computer M1.
Control unit M66 is supplied at pin 11 of connector D - by a line protected by fuse F36 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2 .
Pin 19 connector B and 7 of connector D of M66 are earthed.
The control unit M66 receives the following inputs:
- the "locking" signals from the four knobs, at pin 23 of connector B of and 7 of connector C of M66;
- the locking/unlocking signals from the emergency key pawl, at pins 24 and 25 of connector B of M66;
- the negative signal from the locking/unlocking button, located in the controls on the tunnel H35, at pin 34 of connector A of M66.
According to the control logic illustrated, the control unit M66 controls the geared motors for the four door locks and the fuel flap: the joint power supply for the motors is sent from pins 6 and 5 of connector D; the locking/unlocking motors (B/S) are operated from pins 4 and 2 of connector D; the dead lock motors (DL) for locks N50 and N51 are operated from pins 3 and 1 of connector D. N55, N56.
The signalling LED E40 is lit up by a signal from pin 8 of connector C of M66, whilst a reference earth is sent from pin 6.
The activation of the inertia switch I50 is indicated at pin 17 of connector D of the Body Computer M1 : this signal, as described previously, causes the opening of the doors.

## E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING - DESCRIPTION  [939004658]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING > E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Right hand drive, High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939004658

#### DESCRIPTION
The simultaneous operation of the four door locks takes place via:
- TEG the remote control;
- the locking/unlocking button in the centre console.
The TEG remote has 3 buttons which allow the operation of the central locking system: a button for unlocking the doors, one for locking the vehicle and one for releasing the boot
See descriptions 5520 ENGINE STARTING [→939003530 5520 ENGINE STARTING]
The door unlocking/locking management strategy is carried out by the two door opening controls units and the boot control unit (for the rear doors) which control the effective state of the locks through the signals arriving from the switches in the actual locks and the emergency key pawl (driver's door only) in this way the "locking" command is only carried out with all the doors properly shut and the locks unlocked; conversely, the "unlocking" command is only carried out with the locks locked.
The locks have an additional motor that carries out the dead lock function which allows the interior door opening handles to be mechanically disconnected so that it is no longer possible to open the door from the inside (for example, after having broken the glass in a theft attempt); the dead lock function also inhibits the operation of the door locking/unlocking buttons in the dashboard.
The dead lock function is switched on at the time the doors are locked or by pressing the remote control twice.
An LED next to the two above mentioned controls makes the following signals:
- locking of the locks: the LED lights up for 3 seconds. If some of the doors or the boot are not properly shut at the time when the locks are locked, the LED flashes at 3 Hz for 3 seconds;
- dead lock activation: the LED flashes twice for 0.5 seconds;
- unlocking the locks: the LED goes out.
The instrument panel acquires the door status signal via the CAN and lights up the "doors open" warning light and, at the same time, the information is shown on the display; in addition, if one of the doors or the boot or the bonnet is open and the speed of the vehicle exceeds around 4 km/h, an acoustic warning is also emitted.
It is possible, using the special setup in the instrument panel, to select whether to unlock all the doors or only the driver's front door, whilst all the other doors and the boot remain locked.
It is possible to enable/disable the locking of the doors above a certain speed threshold (20 km/h) using the special setup in the instrument panel: in this case the Body Computer implements the locking of the doors when this threshold is exceeded. When the speed returns below this level, the doors and the boot remain locked; later on, when one of the doors is opened, the function is re-enabled and, if the threshold is exceeded, the doors are locked once again.
The boot unlocking operating mode can be selected still using the special setup in the instrument panel:
- assisted boot unlocking: the tailgate is considered as a fifth door to all intents and purposes;
- independent boot unlocking: the boot is locked when the doors are locked, whilst it can be unlocked independently of the unlocking of the doors.
See E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING - DESCRIPTION [→939005505]
The doors are automatically unlocked if the inertia switch is operated: the instrument panel receives a signal from the switch, lights up the appropriate warning light and notifies the Body Computer via the CAN.
The central locking circuit is protected by two specific fuses - one for the front doors and one for the rear doors - located in the junction unit under the dashboard.

## E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939004659]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING > E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Right hand drive, High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939004659

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The door locking/unlocking function is controlled by the control units for the driver's door M66, passenger side M67 and luggage compartment M63 all connected via the CAN line to one another and to the Body Computer M1.
The control units M66 and M67 receive a power supply at pin 11 of connector D from the line protected by fuse F32 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2, the luggage compartment junction unit M63 at pin B8 of connector A from the line protected by fuse F36 of B2.
Pin 19 connector B and 7 of connector D of M66 and of M67 are earthed.
Pin C8 of connector A of M63 is also earthed.
Control units M66 and M67 receive the following input:
- the "locking" signals from the knobs at pin 23 of connector B of M66 and M67; (the knobs for the rear doors send the signal to the passenger side control unit M67;
- the locking/unlocking signals from the emergency key pawl, at pins 24 and 25 of connector B of M66;
- the negative signal from the locking/unlocking button, located in the controls on the tunnel H35, at pin 34 of connector A of M66.
Similarly the control unit M63 receives control signals from pins 10, 11 and 26 of connector B of M67 and controls the geared motors for the rear door locks: the joint power supply for the motors is sent from pin A7 of connector A and A2 of connector B; the locking/unlocking motors (B/S) are operated from pin C7 of connector A and C2 of connector B; the dead lock motors (DL) for locks N55 and N56 are operated from pin C6 of connector A and C4 of connector B.
The signalling LED E40 is lit up by a signal from pin 8 of connector C of M66, whilst a reference earth is sent from pin 6.
The activation of the inertia switch I50 is indicated at pin 17 of connector D of the Body Computer M1 : this signal, as described previously, causes the opening of the doors.

## E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939004664]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING > E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Right hand drive, Low setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939004664

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The locking/unlocking function for the doors is operated by the front doors control unit M66 connected via the CAN line to the Body Computer M1.
Control unit M66 is supplied at pin 11 of connector D - by a line protected by fuse F36 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2 .
Pin 19 connector B and 7 of connector D of M66 are earthed.
The control unit M66 receives the following inputs:
- the "locking" signals from the four knobs, at pin 23 of connector B of and 7 of connector C of M66;
- the locking/unlocking signals from the emergency key pawl, at pins 24 and 25 of connector B of M66;
- the negative signal from the locking/unlocking button, located in the controls on the tunnel H35, at pin 34 of connector A of M66.
According to the control logic illustrated, the control unit M66 controls the geared motors for the four door locks and the fuel flap: the joint power supply for the motors is sent from pins 6 and 5 of connector D; the locking/unlocking motors (B/S) are operated from pins 4 and 2 of connector D; the dead lock motors (DL) for locks N50 and N51 are operated from pins 3 and 1 of connector D. N55, N56.
The signalling LED E40 is lit up by a signal from pin 8 of connector C of M66, whilst a reference earth is sent from pin 6.
The activation of the inertia switch I50 is indicated at pin 17 of connector D of the Body Computer M1 : this signal, as described previously, causes the opening of the doors.

## E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING - DESCRIPTION  [939011606]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING > E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011606

#### DESCRIPTION
The simultaneous operation of the four door locks takes place via:
- TEG the remote control;
- the locking/unlocking button in the centre console.
The TEG remote has 3 buttons which allow the operation of the central locking system: a button for unlocking the doors, one for locking the vehicle and one for releasing the boot
See descriptions 5520 ENGINE STARTING [→939003530 5520 ENGINE STARTING]
The door unlocking/locking management strategy is carried out by the two door opening controls units and the boot control unit (for the rear doors) which control the effective state of the locks through the signals arriving from the switches in the actual locks and the emergency key pawl (driver's door only) in this way the "locking" command is only carried out with all the doors properly shut and the locks unlocked; conversely, the "unlocking" command is only carried out with the locks locked.
The locks have an additional motor that carries out the dead lock function which allows the interior door opening handles to be mechanically disconnected so that it is no longer possible to open the door from the inside (for example, after having broken the glass in a theft attempt); the dead lock function also inhibits the operation of the door locking/unlocking buttons in the dashboard.
The dead lock function is switched on at the time the doors are locked or by pressing the remote control twice.
An LED next to the two above mentioned controls makes the following signals:
- locking of the locks: the LED lights up for 3 seconds. If some of the doors or the boot are not properly shut at the time when the locks are locked, the LED flashes at 3 Hz for 3 seconds;
- dead lock activation: the LED flashes twice for 0.5 seconds;
- unlocking the locks: the LED goes out.
The instrument panel acquires the door status signal via the CAN and lights up the "doors open" warning light and, at the same time, the information is shown on the display; in addition, if one of the doors or the boot or the bonnet is open and the speed of the vehicle exceeds around 4 km/h, an acoustic warning is also emitted.
It is possible, using the special setup in the instrument panel, to select whether to unlock all the doors or only the driver's front door, whilst all the other doors and the boot remain locked.
It is possible to enable/disable the locking of the doors above a certain speed threshold (20 km/h) using the special setup in the instrument panel: in this case the Body Computer implements the locking of the doors when this threshold is exceeded. When the speed returns below this level, the doors and the boot remain locked; later on, when one of the doors is opened, the function is re-enabled and, if the threshold is exceeded, the doors are locked once again.
The boot unlocking operating mode can be selected still using the special setup in the instrument panel:
- assisted boot unlocking: the tailgate is considered as a fifth door to all intents and purposes;
- independent boot unlocking: the boot is locked when the doors are locked, whilst it can be unlocked independently of the unlocking of the doors.
See E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING - DESCRIPTION [→939005505]
The doors are automatically unlocked if the inertia switch is operated: the instrument panel receives a signal from the switch, lights up the appropriate warning light and notifies the Body Computer via the CAN.
The central locking circuit is protected by two specific fuses - one for the front doors and one for the rear doors - located in the junction unit under the dashboard.

## E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011607]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING > E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011607

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The door locking/unlocking function is controlled by the control units for the driver's door M66, passenger side M67 and luggage compartment M63 all connected via the CAN line to one another and to the Body Computer M1.
The control units M66 and M67 receive a power supply at pin 11 of connector D from the line protected by fuse F32 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2, the luggage compartment junction unit M63 at pin B8 of connector A from the line protected by fuse F36 of B2.
Pin 19 connector B and 7 of connector D of M66 and of M67 are earthed.
Pin C8 of connector A of M63 is also earthed.
Control units M66 and M67 receive the following input:
- the "locking" signals from the knobs at pin 23 of connector B of M66 and M67; (the knobs for the rear doors send the signal to the passenger side control unit M67;
- the locking/unlocking signals from the emergency key pawl, at pins 24 and 25 of connector B of M66;
- the negative signal from the locking/unlocking button, located in the controls on the tunnel H35, at pin 34 of connector A of M66.
Similarly the control unit M63 receives control signals from pins 10, 11 and 26 of connector B of M67 and controls the geared motors for the rear door locks: the joint power supply for the motors is sent from pin A7 of connector A and A2 of connector B; the locking/unlocking motors (B/S) are operated from pin C7 of connector A and C2 of connector B; the dead lock motors (DL) for locks N55 and N56 are operated from pin C6 of connector A and C4 of connector B.
The signalling LED E40 is lit up by a signal from pin 8 of connector C of M66, whilst a reference earth is sent from pin 6.
The activation of the inertia switch I50 is indicated at pin 17 of connector D of the Body Computer M1 : this signal, as described previously, causes the opening of the doors.

## E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING - DESCRIPTION  [939005505]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING > E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Station Wagon
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939005505

#### DESCRIPTION
The boot opening geared motor is operated by:
- the special button in the courtesy light;
- the remote control (TEG).
Operation through the remote control takes place in two ways.
- indepedently of the doors: there is a special button on the remote control that allows the boot only to be "unlocked": the boot is released and lifts up slightly. The operation is signalled by the direction indicators flashing twice; when it is closed again the boot returns to the state prior to opening.
- together and at the same time as the unlocking of the doors: the tailgate is considered as a fifth door to all intents and purposes: for the control logic.
See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING [→939003023]
One of the two modes described above can be selected using a special setup in the instrument panel.
The boot opening function via the button in the courtesy light is disabled (the boot does not open) if the speed of the vehicle is above 10 km/h.
The fuel flap is managed directly by the driver's door node and is therefore connected to the locked/unlocked status of the driver's door.
The boot opening circuit is protected by a specific fuse, located in the junction unit under the dashboard.

## E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING - OPERATIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939005506]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING > E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING - OPERATIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Station Wagon
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939005506

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The "boot open" signal is sent by the switch - located in the courtesy light G10 - to pin 35 of connector E of the Body Computer M1.
According to the control logic illustrated, the Body Computer M1 implements the boot release positive control function from pin 11 of connector F - via the line supplied by fuse F38 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2, pin 18 of connector D - controlling the operation of the boot lock geared motor N57.
The boot unlocking function, inside the Body Computer M1 pin 1 of connector F also has a dedicated earth connection: pin 20 of connector F.
The "boot not properly shut" signal is sent from the switch located in N57 to pin 24 of connector E.
> Note: the contact in question signals the "boot not properly shut" condition; the switch is fitted with another contact that signals the "boot open" condition, a contact used by the boot light functionSee E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - BOOT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT - DESCRIPTION [→939005463]
The fuel flap opening motor N58 is operated by the same control logic as the driver's front door lock, from pins 1 and 2 of connector D of M66. (HIGH version) or from pins 4 and 6 of connector D of M66 LOW version);
See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING [→939003023]
Control unit M66 is supplied at pin 11 of connector D - by a line protected by fuse F32 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2 .
Pin 7 of connector D of M086 is earthed.

## E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING - DESCRIPTION  [939011616]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING > E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011616

#### DESCRIPTION
The boot opening geared motor is operated by:
- the special button in the courtesy light;
- the remote control (TEG).
Operation through the remote control takes place in two ways.
- indepedently of the doors: there is a special button on the remote control that allows the boot only to be "unlocked": the boot is released and lifts up slightly. The operation is signalled by the direction indicators flashing twice; when it is closed again the boot returns to the state prior to opening.
- together and at the same time as the unlocking of the doors: the tailgate is considered as a fifth door to all intents and purposes: for the control logic.
See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING [→939003023]
One of the two modes described above can be selected using a special setup in the instrument panel.
The boot opening function via the button in the courtesy light is disabled (the boot does not open) if the speed of the vehicle is above 10 km/h.
The fuel flap is managed directly by the driver's door node and is therefore connected to the locked/unlocked status of the driver's door.
The boot opening circuit is protected by a specific fuse, located in the junction unit under the dashboard.

## E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING - OPERATIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011617]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING > E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING - OPERATIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011617

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The "boot open" signal is sent by the switch - located in the courtesy light G10 - to pin 35 of connector E of the Body Computer M1.
According to the control logic illustrated, the Body Computer M1 implements the boot release positive control function from pin 11 of connector F - via the line supplied by fuse F38 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2, pin 18 of connector D - controlling the operation of the boot lock geared motor N57.
The boot unlocking function, inside the Body Computer M1 pin 1 of connector F also has a dedicated earth connection: pin 20 of connector F.
The "boot not properly shut" signal is sent from the switch located in N57 to pin 24 of connector E.
> Note: the contact in question signals the "boot not properly shut" condition; the switch is fitted with another contact that signals the "boot open" condition, a contact used by the boot light functionSee E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - BOOT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT - DESCRIPTION [→939005463]
The fuel flap opening motor N58 is operated by the same control logic as the driver's front door lock, from pins 1 and 2 of connector D of M66. (HIGH version) or from pins 4 and 6 of connector D of M66 LOW version);
See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING [→939003023]
Control unit M66 is supplied at pin 11 of connector D - by a line protected by fuse F32 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2 .
Pin 7 of connector D of M086 is earthed.

## E3050 FRONT ELECTRIC WINDOWS - DESCRIPTION  [939011626]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3050 ELECTRIC FRONT WINDOWS > E3050 FRONT ELECTRIC WINDOWS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Low setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011626

#### DESCRIPTION
The electric windows for the front doors are operated through the switches on the driver's door (both windows) and the passenger side (passenger side only).
The control units in the door control the operation of the driver's and passenger side electric window motors which are operated both manually and automatically depending on the version.
Automatic operation takes place as follows:
- if the button is pressed is between 60 and 300 milliseconds, operation is manual. the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed;
- f the key is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds, operation is automatic: even if the button is released, the glass continues to move up/down until the end of travel position is reached or until the intervention of the anti-crush safety system (if fitted);
- pressing the button again whilst the window is moving stops it in the position it is in;
- if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock).
The windows are automatically opened or closed through the special prolonged (more than 2 seconds) command sent by the TEG remote control button.
The circuit is controlled by the services relay and protected by two fuses located in the junction unit under the dashboard: there is a power supply both with the TEG inserted (ON) and not inserted (OFF); during the starting stage this relay is temporarily deactivated whilst with the TEG not inserted (OFF) the Body Computer keeps the relay activated for 3 minutes but deactivates it 30 seconds after one of the doors is opened.
The driver's door control unit acquires both the driver's front door and passenger side front door commands; it manages the movement of the driver's window directly and sends the relevant movement commands for the passenger side window via the CAN to the passenger door control unit which manages the passenger side window directly.

## E3050 FRONT ELECTRIC WINDOWS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011627]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3050 ELECTRIC FRONT WINDOWS > E3050 FRONT ELECTRIC WINDOWS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Low setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011627

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
Service relay T13, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B2 , supplies the driver's door control unit M66 - pin 8 of connector D and the passenger side control unit M67 - pin 8 of connector A , in accordance with the logic described above and controlled by the Body Computer M1, via two lines, protected by fuses F47 and F48. Pin 19 connector B and 7 of connector D of M66 and pin 7 of connector A of M67 are earthed. Control unit M66 is connected to the Body Computer M1 via the CAN line.
Unit H44 contains the driver and passenger side window controls:: dedicated analogue signals are sent to pins 31 and 32 of connector A of M66 (pin 33 supplies a reference earth).. Similarly, the control at the front passenger door H50 sends a dedicated analogue signal to control unit M66 pins 1 and 4 of connector C.
Cotnrol unit M66 controls the motor N60 (driver's side) directly - pins 9 and 10 of connector D. The commands for motor N61 (passenger side) are sent from pins 2 and 3 of connector C via the control unit M67 from pins 9 and 10 of connector A.

## E3050 FRONT ELECTRIC WINDOWS - DESCRIPTION  [939004668]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3050 ELECTRIC FRONT WINDOWS > E3050 FRONT ELECTRIC WINDOWS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Right hand drive, High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939004668

#### DESCRIPTION
The electric windows for the front doors are operated through the switches on the driver's door (both windows) and the passenger side (passenger side only).
The control units in the door control the operation of the driver's and passenger side electric window motors which are operated both manually and automatically depending on the version.
Automatic operation takes place as follows:
- if the button is pressed is between 60 and 300 milliseconds, operation is manual. the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed;
- f the key is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds, operation is automatic: even if the button is released, the glass continues to move up/down until the end of travel position is reached or until the intervention of the anti-crush safety system (if fitted);
- pressing the button again whilst the window is moving stops it in the position it is in;
- if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock).
Each control unit in the door also manages the anti-crush safety function: it acquires information concerning the possible presence of an obstacle whilst the glass is closing (upwards movement): a resistive sensor is inserted in an outer casing fitted to the upper seal which is compressed if there is an obstacle preventing the window from closing properly: under these circumstances the control unit immediately interrupts the travel of the glass and reverses it until it is in the bottom end of travel position. The correct operation of the anti-crush sensor is controlled by the control unit check function: in the case of a failure this information is sent via the CAN to the instrument panel to show the information on the display.
In addition, if a fault is detected, the control unit inhibits the automatic raising operation only allowing it in steps of 500 ms each time the button is pressed.
The windows are automatically opened or closed through the special prolonged (more than 2 seconds) command sent by the TEG remote control button.
The circuit is controlled by the services relay and protected by two fuses located in the junction unit under the dashboard: there is a power supply both with the TEG inserted (ON) and not inserted (OFF); during the starting stage this relay is temporarily deactivated whilst with the TEG not inserted (OFF) the Body Computer keeps the relay activated for 3 minutes but deactivates it 30 seconds after one of the doors is opened.
The driver's door control unit acquires both the driver's front door and passenger side front door commands; it manages the movement of the driver's window directly and sends the relevant movement commands for the passenger side window via the CAN to the passenger door control unit which manages the passenger side window directly.

## E3050 FRONT ELECTRIC WINDOWS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939004669]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3050 ELECTRIC FRONT WINDOWS > E3050 FRONT ELECTRIC WINDOWS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Right hand drive, High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939004669

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The services relay T13, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B2, supplies pin 14 of connector F, the two control units for the driver's door M66 and the passenger door M67, pin 8 of connector D, through the control logic described above and controlled by the Body Computer M1, via two lines protected by fuses F47 and F48. Pins 19 of connector B and 7 of connector D of M66 and M67 are earthed. Control units M66 and M67 are connected via the CAN line to one another and to the Body Computer M1.
Unit H44 contains the driver and passenger side window controls:: dedicated analogue signals are sent to pins 31 and 32 of connector A of M66 (pin 33 supplies a reference earth).. Similarly, the control at the passenger front door H50 sends a special analogue signal to the control unit M67 pin 32 (pin 33 provides the reference earth).
Control unit M66 operates the motor N60 (driver's side) directly - pins 9 and 10 of connector D - and via control unit M67 - pins 9 and 19 of connector D - motor N61 (passenger side).
Pins 2 and 5 of connector C of M66 and M67 also receive signals from the anti-crush safety sensors K22 and K23 .
The two control units are connected to the instrument panel E50 via the CAN line to manage the signal if there is a failure in the anti-crush safety sensors.
