## E3050 FRONT ELECTRIC WINDOWS - DESCRIPTION  [939004673]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3050 ELECTRIC FRONT WINDOWS > E3050 FRONT ELECTRIC WINDOWS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Right hand drive, Low setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939004673

#### DESCRIPTION
The electric windows for the front doors are operated through the switches on the driver's door (both windows) and the passenger side (passenger side only).
The control units in the door control the operation of the driver's and passenger side electric window motors which are operated both manually and automatically depending on the version.
Automatic operation takes place as follows:
- if the button is pressed is between 60 and 300 milliseconds, operation is manual. the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed;
- f the key is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds, operation is automatic: even if the button is released, the glass continues to move up/down until the end of travel position is reached or until the intervention of the anti-crush safety system (if fitted);
- pressing the button again whilst the window is moving stops it in the position it is in;
- if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock).
The windows are automatically opened or closed through the special prolonged (more than 2 seconds) command sent by the TEG remote control button.
The circuit is controlled by the services relay and protected by two fuses located in the junction unit under the dashboard: there is a power supply both with the TEG inserted (ON) and not inserted (OFF); during the starting stage this relay is temporarily deactivated whilst with the TEG not inserted (OFF) the Body Computer keeps the relay activated for 3 minutes but deactivates it 30 seconds after one of the doors is opened.
The driver's door control unit acquires both the driver's front door and passenger side front door commands; it manages the movement of the driver's window directly and sends the relevant movement commands for the passenger side window via the CAN to the passenger door control unit which manages the passenger side window directly.

## E3050 FRONT ELECTRIC WINDOWS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939004674]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3050 ELECTRIC FRONT WINDOWS > E3050 FRONT ELECTRIC WINDOWS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Right hand drive, Low setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939004674

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
Service relay T13, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B2 , supplies the driver's door control unit M66 - pin 8 of connector D and the passenger side control unit M67 - pin 8 of connector A , in accordance with the logic described above and controlled by the Body Computer M1, via two lines, protected by fuses F47 and F48. Pin 19 connector B and 7 of connector D of M66 and pin 7 of connector A of M67 are earthed. Control unit M66 is connected to the Body Computer M1 via the CAN line.
Unit H44 contains the driver and passenger side window controls:: dedicated analogue signals are sent to pins 31 and 32 of connector A of M66 (pin 33 supplies a reference earth).. Similarly, the control at the front passenger door H50 sends a dedicated analogue signal to control unit M66 pins 1 and 4 of connector C.
Cotnrol unit M66 controls the motor N60 (driver's side) directly - pins 9 and 10 of connector D. The commands for motor N61 (passenger side) are sent from pins 2 and 3 of connector C via the control unit M67 from pins 9 and 10 of connector A.

## E3050 FRONT ELECTRIC WINDOWS - DESCRIPTION  [939011621]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3050 ELECTRIC FRONT WINDOWS > E3050 FRONT ELECTRIC WINDOWS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011621

#### DESCRIPTION
The electric windows for the front doors are operated through the switches on the driver's door (both windows) and the passenger side (passenger side only).
The control units in the door control the operation of the driver's and passenger side electric window motors which are operated both manually and automatically depending on the version.
Automatic operation takes place as follows:
- if the button is pressed is between 60 and 300 milliseconds, operation is manual. the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed;
- f the key is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds, operation is automatic: even if the button is released, the glass continues to move up/down until the end of travel position is reached or until the intervention of the anti-crush safety system (if fitted);
- pressing the button again whilst the window is moving stops it in the position it is in;
- if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock).
Each control unit in the door also manages the anti-crush safety function: it acquires information concerning the possible presence of an obstacle whilst the glass is closing (upwards movement): a resistive sensor is inserted in an outer casing fitted to the upper seal which is compressed if there is an obstacle preventing the window from closing properly: under these circumstances the control unit immediately interrupts the travel of the glass and reverses it until it is in the bottom end of travel position. The correct operation of the anti-crush sensor is controlled by the control unit check function: in the case of a failure this information is sent via the CAN to the instrument panel to show the information on the display.
In addition, if a fault is detected, the control unit inhibits the automatic raising operation only allowing it in steps of 500 ms each time the button is pressed.
The windows are automatically opened or closed through the special prolonged (more than 2 seconds) command sent by the TEG remote control button.
The circuit is controlled by the services relay and protected by two fuses located in the junction unit under the dashboard: there is a power supply both with the TEG inserted (ON) and not inserted (OFF); during the starting stage this relay is temporarily deactivated whilst with the TEG not inserted (OFF) the Body Computer keeps the relay activated for 3 minutes but deactivates it 30 seconds after one of the doors is opened.
The driver's door control unit acquires both the driver's front door and passenger side front door commands; it manages the movement of the driver's window directly and sends the relevant movement commands for the passenger side window via the CAN to the passenger door control unit which manages the passenger side window directly.

## E3050 FRONT ELECTRIC WINDOWS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011622]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3050 ELECTRIC FRONT WINDOWS > E3050 FRONT ELECTRIC WINDOWS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011622

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The services relay T13, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B2, supplies pin 14 of connector F, the two control units for the driver's door M66 and the passenger door M67, pin 8 of connector D, through the control logic described above and controlled by the Body Computer M1, via two lines protected by fuses F47 and F48. Pins 19 of connector B and 7 of connector D of M66 and M67 are earthed. Control units M66 and M67 are connected via the CAN line to one another and to the Body Computer M1.
Unit H44 contains the driver and passenger side window controls:: dedicated analogue signals are sent to pins 31 and 32 of connector A of M66 (pin 33 supplies a reference earth).. Similarly, the control at the passenger front door H50 sends a special analogue signal to the control unit M67 pin 32 (pin 33 provides the reference earth).
Control unit M66 operates the motor N60 (driver's side) directly - pins 9 and 10 of connector D - and via control unit M67 - pins 9 and 19 of connector D - motor N61 (passenger side).
Pins 2 and 5 of connector C of M66 and M67 also receive signals from the anti-crush safety sensors K22 and K23 .
The two control units are connected to the instrument panel E50 via the CAN line to manage the signal if there is a failure in the anti-crush safety sensors.

## E3051 ELECTRIC REAR WINDOWS - DESCRIPTION  [939011631]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3051 ELECTRIC REAR WINDOWS > E3051 ELECTRIC REAR WINDOWS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011631

#### DESCRIPTION
The electric windows in the rear doors are activated using the switches in the actual doors and the driver's front door.
The luggage compartment junction unit checks the operation of the rear electric window motors directly.
The commands from the driver's front door are transmitted via the CAN from the control unit in the door.
The electric window motors are operated either manually or automatically, depending on the trim level.
Automatic operation takes place as follows:
- if the button is pressed is between 60 and 300 milliseconds, operation is manual. the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed;
- f the key is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds, operation is automatic: even if the button is released, the glass continues to move up/down until the end of travel position is reached or until the intervention of the anti-crush safety system (if fitted);
- pressing the button again whilst the window is moving stops it in the position it is in;
- if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock).
The luggage compartment junction unit also manages the anti-crush safety function: it acquires information concerning the possible presence of an obstacle whilst the glass is closing (upwards movement): a resistive sensor is inserted in an outer casing fitted to the upper seal which is compressed if there is an obstacle preventing the window from closing properly: under these circumstances the control unit immediately interrupts the travel of the window and reverses it to the lower end of travel position.
The correct operation of the anti-crush sensor is controlled by the control unit check function: in the case of a failure this information is sent via the CAN to the instrument panel to show the information on the display.
In addition, if a fault is detected, the control unit inhibits the automatic raising operation only allowing it in steps of 500ms each time the button is pressed.
The circuit is operated according to the luggage compartment junction unit control logic with a power supply protected by two special fuses operated by the underdashboard junction unit services relay: there is a power supply both with the TEG inserted (ON) and not inserted (OFF); during the starting stage this relay is temporarily deactivated whilst with the TEG not inserted (OFF) the Body Computer keeps the relay activated for 3 minutes but deactivates it 30 seconds after one of the doors is opened.
The windows are automatically opened or closed through the special prolonged (more than 2 seconds) command sent by the TEG remote control button.

## E3051 ELECTRIC REAR WINDOWS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011632]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3051 ELECTRIC REAR WINDOWS > E3051 ELECTRIC REAR WINDOWS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011632

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The services relay T13, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B2, supplies the luggage compartment junction unit (which manages the rear electric windows) M63 pin A8 of connector A and pin B8 of connector B, with the logic described above and controlled by the Body Computer M1 pin 14 of connector F, via two lines protected by fuses F33 and F34 of B2.
Pins B1 and C8 of connector A and pin A1 of connector B of M63 are earthed.
The junction unit is connected via the CAN line to the driver's front door control unit M66.
The unit H44 also incorporates the controls for the rear windows and the LOCK button: special analogue signals are sent to pins 27 of connector B and 1 and 3 of connector C of M66 (pin 33 of connector A provides the reference earth).
With the LOCK button pressed the control unit M66 relays the signal for switching on the relevant LED in H44 (from pin 7 of connector C); the control unit M66 then transmits these signals to control unit M63 via the CAN.
Similarly, the controls at the rear doors H53 and H54 send dedicated analogue signals to the control unit M63 to pins B5 of connectors A and B.
The control unit M63 operates the motors N65 (left) - from pins A1 and C1 of connector A and N66 (right) - from pins A8 and C8 of connector B.
The signals for the anti-crush sensors K19 and K24 reach pins A5 and B3 of connector A of M63 and pins A4 and A6 of connector B of M63.
The control units M63 is also connected via the CAN line to the Body Computer M1 and to the instrument panel E50 to manage the signal if there is a failure in the anti-crush safety sensors.

## E3060 SUN ROOF - DESCRIPTION  [939011636]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3060 SUN ROOF > E3060 SUN ROOF - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Powered sunroof
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011636

#### DESCRIPTION
The sun-roof provides a means of extra passenger compartment ventilation and ensures swift air exchange when necessary for improved passenger comfort.
The system is operated by a knob near the front courtesy light.
The roof operating strategy is controlled by a special control unit that receives signals from the control knob and the roof operating motor.
When the control knob is turned in the direction shown by the arrow, the roof slides open: a choice of 5 opening positions is available; return the knob to the central position to close the roof.
The sun-roof is equipped with a blind underneath that slides manually but is pushed along by the roof when it opens. The blind emerges slightly when the roof is closed to provide access to the manoeuvring handle.
When the control handle is turned the opposite way to the direction shown by the arrow, the roof swivels up at the rear: a choice of 3 opening positions is available; return the knob to the central position to close the roof.
Press the knob to interrupt all movement (inhibition position).
The electronic roof control circuit also includes an antipinch function: whilst the roof is being closed, themovement is interrupted and reversed by about 10 cm if an obstacle is dtected by a Hall effect sensor located on the motor. This function can be excluded for safety reasons by pressing the knob as described above.
The sun roof is also automatically opened through the special prolonged (more than 2 seconds) command sent by the TEG remote control button.
The sun roof is also automatically closed - if left open - through the special prolonged (more than 2 seconds) command sent by the TEG remote control button.
The circuit is controlled by the services relay and protected by a specific fuse, both located in the junction unit under the dashboard: there is a power supply both with the TEG inserted (ON) and not inserted (OFF) during the starting stage this relay is temporarily deactivated whilst with the TEG not inserted (OFF) the Body Computer keeps the relay activated for 3 minutes but deactivates it 30 seconds after one of the doors is opened.

## E3060 SUN ROOF - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011637]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3060 SUN ROOF > E3060 SUN ROOF - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Powered sunroof
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011637

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The services relay T13, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B2, supplies the sun roof control motor N35 - pin 7 - via the line protected by fuse F46 of B2 through the logic described above and controlled by the Body Computer M1.
The roof moving enablement/go ahead signal reaches pin 9 of N35 in accordance with the logic described above coming from pin 10 of connector D of the Body Computer M1.
Pin 8 of N35 receives the speedometer signal from pin 28 of connector B of the Body Computer M1.
Pin 10 of N35 is earthed, whilst pin 1 of N35 sends a power supply to switch H60 which relays the various control signals corresponding to the various positions of the knob to pins 2, 3, 4 and 5 of N35.

## E3070 CIGAR LIGHTER/ CURRENT SOCKET - DESCRIPTION  [939011641]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3070 CIGAR LIGHTER / CURRENT SOCKET > E3070 CIGAR LIGHTER/ CURRENT SOCKET - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011641

#### DESCRIPTION
There is a standard type current socket on the tunnel console next to the handbrake, which can be used for the cigar lighter or for connecting instruments or equipment operating on 12 V.
There is a second current socket the same as the first one in the end section of the tunnel console towards the rear seats.
In the STATION WAGON version there is also a third current socket similar to the other two, located on the left-hand side of the luggage compartment.
The cigar lighter heater coil can be placed in the front socket of the console; simply press the knob to operate it: after a few seconds it will come out automatically, ready for use.
The two sockets on the console have a ring nut that lights up when the side lights are on.
See E2535 CONTROL LIGHTS [→939002993]
The sockets are equipped with a thermal protection device: this protection cuts off the power supply if devices that absorb a lot of energy are connected.
The circuit for the two current sockets in the console is protected by a specific fuse and controlled by the ignition-operated exclusion relay located in the junction unit under the dashboard. These sockets are ignition-operated (INT/A), to prevent the battery from being run down.
The circuit for the luggage compartment current socket is also controlled by an ignition-operated (INT/A) exclusion relay and protected by a specific fuse, located in the luggage compartment fuse box.

## E3070 CIGAR LIGHTER/ CURRENT SOCKET - OPERATIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011642]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3070 CIGAR LIGHTER / CURRENT SOCKET > E3070 CIGAR LIGHTER/ CURRENT SOCKET - OPERATIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011642

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
Current socket/ cigar lighter P50 and the one at the back on the tunnel P51 receive a power supply from the ignition-controlled line (INT/A) of relay T12 and are protected by fuses F44 and F52 respectively, both housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B2.
In the STATION WAGON version the rear current socket P52 power supply arrives via the relay T21 located in the fuse box in the boot B45; this is energized by the ignition-controlled line (INT/A) which arrives directly from the steering lock node M89; fuse F55, also located in B45, protects the P52 power supply circuit.
Unlike the other two, the rear current socket does not have a ring nut that lights up when the side lights are switched on.

## E3075 HEATED SEATS - DESCRIPTION  [939011646]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3075 HEATED SEATS > E3075 HEATED SEATS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011646

#### DESCRIPTION
The front seats are available, on request, with a special heating system (comprising two heating elements located in the cushion and the backrest): this allows the seat to be heated to overcome the discomfort of cold passenger compartments in very harsh climates, e.g. when the car is left in the open for long periods in winter.
The heating device located in each seat consists of two resistors activated by a controls located on the outside of each seat: there is a ring nut through which the function is switched on/off and the heating is adjusted to 3 different settings (0 = seat heating switched off).
Once a certain temperature has been reached the heating stops automatically thanks to a thermal contact inside the actual device.
A special LED in the actual switches indicates that the resistances are switched on.
The seat heating can only be activated with the ignition on (INT/A).
The seat heating circuit is controlled by a special relay and protected by two specific fuses located in the fuse box in the boot.

## E3075 HEATED SEATS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011647]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3075 HEATED SEATS > E3075 HEATED SEATS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011647

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The seat heating power supply arrives via the relay T21 located in the fuse box in the boot B45; this is energized by the ignition-controlled line (INT/A) which arrives directly from the steering lock node M89; fuses F57 and F67, located in B45, protect the supply circuit for the two seats: the power supply for the two heaters O40 and O41 takes place via the control units M170 and M110 which receive commands from the switches I65 and I66.
The switches are lit up with the ignition on (INT) by the line for fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2.

## E3076 ELECTRICALLY ADJUSTABLE SEATS - DESCRIPTION  [939011651]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3076 ELECTRICALLY-ADJUSTABLE SEATS > E3076 ELECTRICALLY ADJUSTABLE SEATS - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011651

#### DESCRIPTION
The vehicle can be fitted with electrically adjustable front seats.
A multifunction control on each seat includes:
- adjustment of the backrest angle;
- lengthwise adjustment of the seat;
- front and rear height adjustment of the seat (rocker).
The system also makes it possible to memorize and recall three different positions for the driver's seat (and the door mirrors): after the position of the seat and the door mirrors has been adjusted, pressing one of the buttons ("1", "2" or "3") for a few seconds memorizes the position; this can only take place with the TEG inserted (ON).
To recall a previously memorized position briefly press the relevant button. When a new seat position is memorized any previously memorized settings on this button are automatically cancelled
> Note: Seat position memorization does not include heating start upSee E3075 HEATED SEATS [→939011645]
> Note: The seat is also equipped with a lumbar adjustment knob that makes it possible to improve comfort by altering the backrest support: this adjustment is always mechanical and not controlled by electric motors.
The seat moving circuit is protected by two specific fuses located in the luggage compartment fuse box.

## E3076 ELECTRICALLY ADJUSTABLE SEATS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011652]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3076 ELECTRICALLY-ADJUSTABLE SEATS > E3076 ELECTRICALLY ADJUSTABLE SEATS - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: High setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011652

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The driver's seat H66 and passenger seat H67 control units control the entire system. The control knobs and buttons for the various functions are built into the control units themselves.
The power supply to H66 and H67 - to pin 9 of connector A - passes through fuses F56 and F60, located in the luggage compartment fuse box B45
Pin 5 of connector A and 8 of connector B of H66 and H67 are earthed.
Pins 5 and 6 of connector B of H66 and H67 are connected to the Body Computer M1 via the CAN.
The two control units N66 and H67 control the various motors that move the seats in accordance with the logic described above:
- adjustment of the backrest angle: motor N132 or N135 controlled;
- lengthwise adjustment (sliding) of the seat: motor N127 or N130 controlled;
- height adjustment of the cushion - front section: motor N125 or N128 controlled;
- height adjustment of the cushion - rear section (rocker): motor N126 or N129 controlled;

## E3080 HEADLIGHT ALIGNMENT ADJUSTMENT - DESCRIPTION  [939011661]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3080 HEADLAMP AGLINMENT CORRECTOR > E3080 HEADLIGHT ALIGNMENT ADJUSTMENT - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Xenon Gas headlamps
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011661

#### DESCRIPTION
The vehicle is fitted with two GAS DISCHARGE headlamps.
The electronics in each of the two headlamps switches the gas discharge bulbs on and off at the times defined by the software and in accordance with international legislation.
The system for each lamp comprises an igniter located at the base of the bulb and a ballast located in the lower part of the lamp.
The left lamp is the master control unit whilst the right one carries out a slave role. The master acquires the command for the dipped headlamps, the vehicle speed and from the potentiometers located on the wheel axles.
Depending on the inputs, the control unit controls the relevant adjustment motor, located in the headlamps, directly and tilts it as appropriate.
For more details
See descriptions 5540 EXTERIOR LIGHTING [→939003542 5540 EXTERIOR LIGHTING]

> Block applies to: all engines; all production periods
> Note: On versions with gas discharge headlamps, the light beam is adjusted automatically and there is no activation of the selector in the panel on the left side.

The device is enabled only with the dipped beams on.
The electronics for the two headlamps receive a supply from a fuse which protects other ignition-controlled power supplies.

## E3080 HEADLIGHT ALIGNMENT ADJUSTMENT - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011662]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3080 HEADLAMP AGLINMENT CORRECTOR > E3080 HEADLIGHT ALIGNMENT ADJUSTMENT - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Xenon Gas headlamps
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011662

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
Both electronic systems inside the headlamps F10 (left) and F11 (right) are supplied - pin 9 - from the INT line of junction unit B2 protected by fuse F37.
Pins 12 of the two control units are connected to one another by means of a special serial line, whilst the speedometer signal from the Body Computer M1 (pin 28 of connector B) reaches pin 10 of the junction unit located in headlamp F10.
Pins 11 of the two headlamps are connected to the diagnostic K line
See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR [→939011851]
The Body Computer M1 controls the supply for the dipped headlamps sending an earth signal to relay T1 in the junction unit under the dashboard B2 from pin 8 of connector F of M1 which energizes relay T1: this supplies the dipped headlamps F10 (left) and F11 (right). Each circuit is protected by a fuse in the junction unit B2 : F13 for the left headlamp and F12 for the right.
The headlamp alignment function, managed by the connection F10B, is incorporated in the headlamp F10: the two sensors (potentiometers) that measure the geometry at the front K1 and at the rear K2 are connected; on the basis of these signals, the headlamp electronics automatically adjust the light beam by means of a special motor (the motor for the left headlamp is regulated directly, whilst the one for the right headlamp is adjusted via the serial line between F10 and F11).

## E3080 HEADLIGHT ALIGNMENT ADJUSTMENT - DESCRIPTION  [939011656]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3080 HEADLAMP AGLINMENT CORRECTOR > E3080 HEADLIGHT ALIGNMENT ADJUSTMENT - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011656

#### DESCRIPTION
The adjustment of the headlamp light beam according to the load is carried out by means of a special device (located inside the front light cluster) which tilts it appropriately, lowering the light beam if the vehicle is heavily laden and raising it if the load lessens.
A special wheel, located in the controls to the left of the steering wheel, allows the adjustment of the headlamps in 4 vertical positions from 0 to 3:
- position 0: one or two persons in the front seats, full fuel tank, fully equipped (vehicle in running order);
- position 1: five persons;
- position 2: five persons with full luggage compartment (about 50 kg);
- position 3: driver and 300 kg load, all stowed in the luggage compartment (full load);
The device is enabled only with the dipped beams on.
The relay which controls the engagement of the dipped headlamps also supplies the adjustment motors inside the headlamps; this relay for switching the dipped headlamps on is managed by the Body Computer: the relay energizing is activated by TEG inserted (INT) enablement signals and by the steering column switch unit dipped headlamps control.

## E3080 HEADLIGHT ALIGNMENT ADJUSTMENT - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011657]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3080 HEADLAMP AGLINMENT CORRECTOR > E3080 HEADLIGHT ALIGNMENT ADJUSTMENT - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011657

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The dipped headlamps activation (earth) signal - and any AUTO function - is sent to pin 2 of connector I and to pin 28 of connector G of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unit H5
See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS [→939002923]
The Body Computer M1 controls the supply for the dipped headlamps sending an earth signal to relay T1 in the junction unit under the dashboard B2 from pin 8 of connector F of M1 which energizes relay T1: the latter supplies the dipped headlamps - pin 2 for the lamps F10 (left) and F11 (right); at the same time it provides the enablement for the adjustment motors - pin 6 for lamps F10 (left) and F11 (right);
Each circuit is protected by a fuse in the junction unit B2 : F13 for the left headlamp and F12 for the right.
The control for the headlamp adjustment, located in the unit to the left of the steering wheel H90, also receives the enablement supply - pin 5 of connector A, whilst a control signal produced by the adjustment potentiometer - pin 15 of connector B is sent; this control signal "passes through" the junction unit under the dashboard B and activates the adjustment motors built into the headlamps - pin 7 for the (left) lamps F10 and F11 (right).

## E3090 PARKING SENSOR - DESCRIPTION  [939011666]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3090 PARKING SENSOR > E3090 PARKING SENSOR - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011666

#### DESCRIPTION
The "Parking Assistance" system supplies the driver with information on distance when approaching obstacles (both behind and in front of the vehicle) thereby providing help with parking manoeuvres and identifying obstacles that are outside the field of vision.
The information concerning the presence or distance of the obstacle is transmitted to the driver by means of acoustic and visual signals:
- the frequency of the acoustic impulse warnings depends on the distance of the obstacle from the bumper.
- the display in the instrument panel shows the areas around the vehicle which start flashing if the system detects that the vehicle is getting close to an obstacle.
The system is activated if the following conditions are present simultaneously:
- Key ON (TEG inserted)
- reverse gear engaged or activation button - located on the front courtesy light - pressed (with the speed below 15 km/h).
When the system is activated the buzzer warns of this condition and the LED is lit up. The system is deactivated:
- by pressing the button again;
- by disengaging reverse gear and when the vehicle speed is above 18 km/h.
The LED goes out when the system is deactivated.
> Note: The distance measurement only takes place when the system is activated, whilst only the control unit is operational in the inactive state.
An electronic control unit activates and controls the operation of the sensors located in the front bumper and in the rear bumper, processes the signals received and operates the buzzers, one at the front and one at the back: the first is located on the cover under the dashboard on the driver's side, the second is located in the luggage compartment at the base of the right rear pillar.
The sensors use ultrasound technology and act as intelligent transmitters/receivers with triangulation technology: allowing improved detection in critical situations or in the presence of small obstacles. The impulses emitted are reflected by any obstacles; the transducer receives an echo which is converted into a digital signal and sent to the electronic control unit.
The signalling of the distance of the obstacle is achieved through sound and visual signals:
- the sound from the buzzer warns the driver that the vehicle is approaching an obstacle: the pause between the sounds is directly proportional to the distance from the obstacle, whilst a continuous sound indicates that the obstacle is less than 30 cm away;
- the instrument panel display with the system activated shows the various areas around the vehicle, 7 front and 8 rear. The various areas are, in the various cases, either off, flashing or on constantly.
For more details and information on the operation of the system,
See descriptions 5580H PARKING OBSTACLE DETECTION DEVICE [→939003539 5580H PARKING OBSTACLE DETECTION DEVICE]
The control unit is equipped with an autodiagnostic function: when switched on the control unit carries out an initial test on the sensors which are then continuously subject to fault diagnosis during the operation of the system.
A fault in only one sensor inhibits the operation of the entire system which is deactivated.
Any faults/errors are signalled in the instrument panel by the relevant warning light coming on and the message in the display.
The system is supplied by the circuit protected by a specific fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard.

## E3090 PARKING SENSOR - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011667]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E30 ELECTRICALLY ACTIVATED DEVICES > E3090 PARKING SENSOR > E3090 PARKING SENSOR - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011667

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The parking sensor control unit M84 receives a supply at pin 1 of connector A from the ignition-controlled INT line protected by fuse F49 of junction unit B2; pin 8 of connector A is earthed.
The control unit is connected, via pins 7 and 4 of connector A and the CAN, to all the other nodes in the same network, for example receiving the information that reverse gear is engaged.
The commands for the display are sent to the instrument panel via the CAN.
The signal from the activation/deactivation button, located in the courtesy light G10, reaches pin 4 of connector A. The positive signal that lights up the LED next to the button is sent from pin 13 of connector A.
The front buzzer P44A is connected to pins 3 and 4 of connector B.
The rear buzzer P44B is connected to pins 1 and 10 of connector A.
The four front parking sensors K97 are connected to connector B of the control unit M84: pin 1 provides the reference earth, pin 2 the power supply, pins 5, 6, 7 and 8 are connected to sensors K97A, K97B, K97C and K97D, respectively.
The four rear parking sensors K97 are connected to connector C of the control unit M84: pin 1 provides the reference earth, pin 6 the power supply, pins 5, 3, 2 and 4 are connected to sensors K97E, K97F, K97G and K97H, respectively.

## E3510 RADIO - DESCRIPTION  [939011677]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E35 RADIO ACCESSORIES > E3510 RADIO > E3510 RADIO - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Connect Nav+
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011677

#### DESCRIPTION
The vehicle is equipped with a radio system comprising:
- radio;
- front speakers (woofers in the doors and tweeters in the dashboard);
- rear speakers located in the doors
- cables connecting the radio with the speakers;
- aerial with support fitted at the rear of the roof with a coaxial connecting cable.
A sophisticated Bose HIFI system with special HIFI speakers and an outside amplifier can also be fitted.

> Block applies to: all engines; all production periods
On the version with the built in "CONNECT NAV +" radio-telephone-navigator the radio is incorporated in the unit.
The aerial has three functions (radio/GSM/GPS) for the operation of the telephone and for the navigator.

The radio is a CAN node through which information is exchanged with the Body Computer and with the other electronic units.
The radio is equipped with an anti-theft system through the connection of the radio at the CAN with the Body Computer; it also manages the volume control linked to the vehicle speed: the volume increases and decreases in relation to the speed of the vehicle: this information reaches the radio node via the CAN.
Some versions are equipped with a series of buttons on the steering wheel: these make it possible to replicate some of the commands which are acquired in the same way by the actual radio.
It is also possible to fit a multi-polar cable connecting the radio to a CD player located in the boot, on the right hand side.
See descriptions 5580P CONNECT PANEL [→939003540 5580P CONNECT PANEL]

## E3510 RADIO - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011678]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E35 RADIO ACCESSORIES > E3510 RADIO > E3510 RADIO - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Connect Nav+
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011678

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
Radio P20 is supplied directly (7 of connector A) from the battery via the line of fuse F23 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 .
The radio P20 receives an ignition-operated (INT) power supply (pin 4 of connector A) via the line for fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2 .
Pin 8 of connector A is earthed.
Pins 1 and 3 of connector A receive the CAN line by which the radio P20 is connected to the Body Computer M1 and the other system nodes.
The radio P20 is connected, via the CAN, to the radio controls on the steering wheel, via the clock spring D47.
See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES [→939011452]
The following cables with signals for the speakers leave connector B of P20:
- pins 5 and 6 to the left front speakers P35 and P45;
- pins 3 and 4 to the right front speakers P36 and P46;
- pins 7 and 8 to the left rear speakers P30 and P47;
- pins 1 and 2 to the right rear speakers P31 and P48;
The aerial P25 is connected to the radio by means of the special coaxial cable.
A connection lead runs from connector E of P20 to CD player P75:. this cable, is divided into two sections: one under the dashboard and one under the passenger compartment lining (coupling D96).

## E3510 RADIO - DESCRIPTION  [939011682]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E35 RADIO ACCESSORIES > E3510 RADIO > E3510 RADIO - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Radio setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011682

#### DESCRIPTION

> Block applies to: all engines; all production periods
The vehicle can be fitted, on request, with a simple preparation, (opt. 082) which includes a simple power supply for the radio not fitted on the vehicle, but installed in the aftermarket in accordance with the following ISO standard pin out: (connector A of P20):
- pin 1: n.c. (mute)
- pin 2: n.c.
- pin 3: n.c.
- pin 5: Bose amplifier presence signal
- pin 6: +lights control lighting
- pin 7: ignition-operated power supply +15
- pin 8: earth
> Note: The radio installed in the AFTERMARKET is therefore not a CAN node through which information is exchanged with the Body Computer and with the other electronic units.

The vehicle is equipped with preparation comprising:
- front speakers (woofers in the doors and tweeters in the dashboard);
- rear speakers located in the doors
- cables connecting the radio with the speakers;
- aerial with support fitted at the rear of the roof with a coaxial connecting cable.
A sophisticated Bose HIFI system with special HIFI speakers and an outside amplifier can also be fitted.

## E3510 RADIO - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011683]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E35 RADIO ACCESSORIES > E3510 RADIO > E3510 RADIO - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Radio setup
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011683

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
Radio P20 is supplied directly (4 of connector A) from the battery via the line of fuse F23 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 .
The radio P20 receives an ignition-operated (INT) power supply (pin 7 of connector A) via the line for fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2 .
Pin 8 of connector A is earthed.
Pin 6 of connector A of P20 receives the power supply for the dimmer lighting, coming from pin 18 of connector H of M1.
See E2535 CONTROL LIGHTS [→939002993]
The following cables with signals for the speakers leave connector B of P20:
- pins 5 and 6 to the left front speakers P35 and P45;
- pins 3 and 4 to the right front speakers P36 and P46;
- pins 7 and 8 to the left rear speakers P30 and P47;
- pins 1 and 2 to the right rear speakers P31 and P48;
The aerial P25 is connected to the radio by means of the special coaxial cable.

## E3510 RADIO - DESCRIPTION  [939011687]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E35 RADIO ACCESSORIES > E3510 RADIO > E3510 RADIO - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: BOSE System
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011687

#### DESCRIPTION
A sophisticated Bose HIFI system with special HIFI speakers and an outside amplifier is available on request.
The system has been developed ad hoc for the vehicle: the acoustic properties of the passenger compartment have been carefully studied so that the amplifier and the speakers are ideally suited to the vehicle: optimum listening is available in any part of the passenger compartment.
Unlike the system fitted as standard, the Bose system offers:
- special speakers at front and rear, which are midwoofers with separate tweeters;
- subwoofer rear speaker located under the rear parcel shelf;
- centerfill speaker located in the centre of the dashboard under the centre air vent;
- high power amplifier located under the rear parcel shelf in the boot.
The system is completed by a microphone, located in the centre courtesy light, which detects background noise in the passenger compartment: the signal is sent for amplification allowing the optimum adjustment and equalizing of the output levels.
The other components (radio, aerial, etc.) are the same as the standard system.
For more details
See descriptions 5570 ACCESSORIES [→939003541 5570 ACCESSORIES]

## E3510 RADIO - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011688]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E35 RADIO ACCESSORIES > E3510 RADIO > E3510 RADIO - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: BOSE System
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011688

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
Radio P20 is supplied directly (pin 4 and 2 of connector A) from the battery via the line of fuse F23 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 .
Pin 8 of connector A is earthed.
Pins 1 and 3 of connector A receive the CAN line by which the radio P20 is connected to the Body Computer M1 and the other system nodes.
The radio P20 is connected, via the CAN, to the radio controls on the steering wheel, via the clock spring D47.
See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES [→939011452]
The amplifier P70 receives a direct supply from the battery - at pin 31 - via the line for fuse F54 of the fuse box in the boot B45; pin 2 of amplifier P70 is earthed.
Pin 6 of P70 is connected via a line to radio P20 - pin 6 of connector C - which supplies a positive signal to enable the amplifier to be switched on.
The cables with signals for the speakers leave from connector B of P20; these signals are sent to the BOSE amplifier P70 which controls the actual speakers:
- pins 5 and 6 of P20 to pins 7 and 19 of P70 and to the left front speakers P35 and P45 - pins 31 and 32 of P70
- pins 3 and 4 of P20 to pins 8 and 20 of P70 and to the right front speakers P36 and P46 - pins 26 and 27 of P70;
- pins 7 and 8 of P20 to pins 9 and 21 of P70 and to the left rear speakers P30 and P47 - pins 4 and 16 of P70;
- pins 1 and 2 of P20 to pins 10 and 22 of P70 and to the right rear speakers P31 and P48 - pins 5 and 37 of P70;
The other signals leaving the BOSE amplifier P70 control the specific speakers:
- centerfill P32 - pins 3 and 15 of P70;
- subwoofer in the rear parcel shelf P49 - pins 11, 12 and 25 of P70; the subwoofer P49 is also supplied via the line for fuse F61 of the fuse box in the boot B45.
The "ambient" microphone located in the front courtesy light G10 - connector E - is connected to pins 29 and 30 of P70.
The aerial P25 is connected to the radio by means of the special coaxial cable.
A connection lead runs from connector E of P20 to CD player P75:. this cable, is divided into two sections: one under the dashboard and one under the passenger compartment lining (coupling D96).

## E3510 RADIO - DESCRIPTION  [939011692]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E35 RADIO ACCESSORIES > E3510 RADIO > E3510 RADIO - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Radio setup, BOSE System
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011692

#### DESCRIPTION
A sophisticated Bose HIFI system with special HIFI speakers and an outside amplifier is available on request.
The system has been developed ad hoc for the vehicle: the acoustic properties of the passenger compartment have been carefully studied so that the amplifier and the speakers are ideally suited to the vehicle: optimum listening is available in any part of the passenger compartment.
Unlike the system fitted as standard, the Bose system offers:
- special speakers at front and rear, which are midwoofers with separate tweeters;
- subwoofer rear speaker located under the rear parcel shelf;
- centerfill speaker located in the centre of the dashboard under the centre air vent;
- high power amplifier located under the rear parcel shelf in the boot.
The system is completed by a microphone, located in the centre courtesy light, which detects background noise in the passenger compartment: the signal is sent for amplification allowing the optimum adjustment and equalizing of the output levels.
The other components (radio, aerial, etc.) are the same as the standard system.
For more details
See descriptions 5570 ACCESSORIES [→939003541 5570 ACCESSORIES]

## E3510 RADIO - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011693]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E35 RADIO ACCESSORIES > E3510 RADIO > E3510 RADIO - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Radio setup, BOSE System
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011693

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
Radio P20 is supplied directly (pin 4 of connector A) from the battery via the line for fuse F23 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 .
The radio P20 receives an ignition-operated (INT) power supply (pin 7 of connector A) via the line for fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2 .
Pin 8 of connector A is earthed.
The amplifier P70 receives a direct supply from the battery - at pin 31 - via the line for fuse F54 of the fuse box in the boot B45; pin 2 of amplifier P70 is earthed.
Pin 6 of P70 is connected via a line to radio P20 - pin 5 of connector A - which supplies a positive signal to enable the amplifier to be switched on.
The cables with signals for the speakers leave from connector B of P20; these signals are sent to the BOSE amplifier P70 which controls the actual speakers:
- pins 5 and 6 of P20 to pins 7 and 19 of P70 and to the left front speakers P35 and P45 - pins 31 and 32 of P70
- pins 3 and 4 of P20 to pins 8 and 20 of P70 and to the right front speakers P36 and P46 - pins 26 and 27 of P70;
- pins 7 and 8 of P20 to pins 9 and 21 of P70 and to the left rear speakers P30 and P47 - pins 4 and 16 of P70;
- pins 1 and 2 of P20 to pins 10 and 22 of P70 and to the right rear speakers P31 and P48 - pins 5 and 37 of P70;
The other signals leaving the BOSE amplifier P70 control the specific speakers:
- centerfill P32 - pins 3 and 15 of P70;
- subwoofer in the rear parcel shelf P49 - pins 11, 12 and 25 of P70; the subwoofer P49 is also supplied via the line for fuse F61 of the fuse box in the boot B45.
The "ambient" microphone located in the front courtesy light G10 - connector E - is connected to pins 29 and 30 of P70.
The aerial P25 is connected to the radio by means of the special coaxial cable.

## E3510 RADIO - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011698]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E35 RADIO ACCESSORIES > E3510 RADIO > E3510 RADIO - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: BOSE System, Connect Nav+
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011698

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
Radio P20 is supplied directly (pin 7 and 2 of connector A) from the battery via the line of fuse F23 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 .
The radio P20 receives an ignition-operated (INT) power supply (pin 4 of connector A) via the line for fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2 .
Pin 8 of connector A is earthed.
Pins 1 and 3 of connector A receive the CAN line by which the radio P20 is connected to the Body Computer M1 and the other system nodes.
The radio P20 is connected, via the CAN, to the radio controls on the steering wheel, via the clock spring D47.
See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES [→939011452]
The amplifier P70 receives a direct supply from the battery - at pin 31 - via the line for fuse F54 of the fuse box in the boot B45; pin 2 of amplifier P70 is earthed.
Pin 6 of P70 is connected via a line to radio P20 - pin 6 of connector C - which supplies a positive signal to enable the amplifier to be switched on.
The cables with signals for the speakers leave from connector B of P20; these signals are sent to the BOSE amplifier P70 which controls the actual speakers:
- pins 5 and 6 of P20 to pins 7 and 19 of P70 and to the left front speakers P35 and P45 - pins 31 and 32 of P70
- pins 3 and 4 of P20 to pins 8 and 20 of P70 and to the right front speakers P36 and P46 - pins 26 and 27 of P70;
- pins 7 and 8 of P20 to pins 9 and 21 of P70 and to the left rear speakers P30 and P47 - pins 4 and 16 of P70;
- pins 1 and 2 of P20 to pins 10 and 22 of P70 and to the right rear speakers P31 and P48 - pins 5 and 37 of P70;
The other signals leaving the BOSE amplifier P70 control the specific speakers:
- centerfill P32 - pins 3 and 15 of P70;
- subwoofer in the rear parcel shelf P49 - pins 11, 12 and 25 of P70; the subwoofer P49 is also supplied via the line for fuse F61 of the fuse box in the boot B45.
The "ambient" microphone located in the front courtesy light G10 - connector E - is connected to pins 29 and 30 of P70.
The aerial P25 is connected to the radio by means of the special coaxial cable.
A connection lead runs from connector E of P20 to CD player P75:. this cable, is divided into two sections: one under the dashboard and one under the passenger compartment lining (coupling D96).

## E3510 RADIO - DESCRIPTION  [939011672]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E35 RADIO ACCESSORIES > E3510 RADIO > E3510 RADIO - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011672

#### DESCRIPTION
The vehicle is equipped with a radio system comprising:
- radio;
- front speakers (woofers in the doors and tweeters in the dashboard);
- rear speakers located in the doors
- cables connecting the radio with the speakers;
- aerial with support fitted at the rear of the roof with a coaxial connecting cable.
A sophisticated Bose HIFI system with special HIFI speakers and an outside amplifier can also be fitted.
The radio is a CAN node through which information is exchanged with the Body Computer and with the other electronic units.
The radio is equipped with an anti-theft system through the connection of the radio at the CAN with the Body Computer; it also manages the volume control linked to the vehicle speed: the volume increases and decreases in relation to the speed of the vehicle: this information reaches the radio node via the CAN.
Some versions are equipped with a series of buttons on the steering wheel: these make it possible to replicate some of the commands which are acquired in the same way by the actual radio.
It is also possible to fit a multi-polar cable connecting the radio to a CD player located in the boot, on the right hand side.
See descriptions 5570 ACCESSORIES [→939003541 5570 ACCESSORIES]

## E3510 RADIO - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011673]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E35 RADIO ACCESSORIES > E3510 RADIO > E3510 RADIO - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011673

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
Radio P20 is supplied directly (4 of connector A) from the battery via the line of fuse F23 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 .
Pin 8 of connector A is earthed.
Pins 1 and 3 of connector A receive the CAN line by which the radio P20 is connected to the Body Computer M1 and the other system nodes.
The radio P20 is connected, via the CAN, to the radio controls on the steering wheel, via the clock spring D47.
See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES [→939011452]
The following cables with signals for the speakers leave connector B of P20:
- pins 5 and 6 to the left front speakers P35 and P45;
- pins 3 and 4 to the right front speakers P36 and P46;
- pins 7 and 8 to the left rear speakers P30 and P47;
- pins 1 and 2 to the right rear speakers P31 and P48;
The aerial P25 is connected to the radio by means of the special coaxial cable.
A connection lead runs from connector E of P20 to CD player P75:. this cable, is divided into two sections: one under the dashboard and one under the passenger compartment lining (coupling D96).

## E3570 BUILT-IN RADIO PHONE - DESCRIPTION  [939004897]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E35 RADIO ACCESSORIES > E3570 INTEGRATED RADIO PHONE > E3570 BUILT-IN RADIO PHONE - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Bluetooth
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939004897

#### DESCRIPTION
The handsfree system for Bluetooth phones - built into the dashboard - allows mobile phones to be used on board whilst assuring customer safety and function.
- Bluetooth receiver;
- integral Voice Recognition unit including microphone (located next to the front courtesy light);
- integral Text to Speech unit.
- USB interface for Media Player.
The control unit is also connected to radio controls on the steering wheel (two special keys for this function are provided in addition to the radio control keys).
The alphanumeric display used is that of the control panel.
See descriptions 5560 INSTRUMENTS [→939003534 5560 INSTRUMENTS]
For more details on system operation
See descriptions 5570 ACCESSORIES [→939003541 5570 ACCESSORIES]

## E3570 BUILT-IN RADIO PHONE - OPERATIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939004898]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E35 RADIO ACCESSORIES > E3570 INTEGRATED RADIO PHONE > E3570 BUILT-IN RADIO PHONE - OPERATIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Bluetooth
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939004898

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The Bluetooth control unit M162 is supplied directly (pin 16 of connector A) from the battery via the line for fuse F39 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2.
The Bluetooth control unit M162 receives an ignition-operated supply (INT) (pin 32 of connector A) via the line for fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2.
Pin 15 of connector A of M162 is earthed.
The CAN line through which the Bluetooth control unit M162 is connected to the radio P20, the controls on the steering wheel - via the clock spring D47 - the Body Computer M1 and the other system nodes, reaches pins 14 and 30 of connector A.
The Bluetooth control unit M162 is connected directly to radio P20 - connector D - from pins 7, 23 and 25 of connector A, sending audio+. audio - and MUTE signals respectively, thus using the radio speakers for voice messages and hands-free communication.
In the version with Media Player USB interface, the Bluetooth control unit M162 is connected to radio P20 - connector C - from pins 5, 22 and 21 of connector A with AUX left, AUX right and AUX earth signals.
The Media Player USB socket P143 is connected to the Bluetooth control unit M162, to pins 3, 4, 19, 20 and 31 respectively, with signals: signal D+, reference earth, signal D-, 5V power supply and shielding.
The hands-free microphone located in the courtesy light G10 is connected to pins 8 and 24 of connector A of M162.

## E3570 BUILT-IN RADIO PHONE - DESCRIPTION  [939011702]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E35 RADIO ACCESSORIES > E3570 INTEGRATED RADIO PHONE > E3570 BUILT-IN RADIO PHONE - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Connect Nav+
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011702

#### DESCRIPTION
In the specification with built in CONNECT NAV + radio-phone-navigation system, the phone (GSM module and SIM-CARD reader) is built into the system.
The system includes:
- GSM module and SIM-CARD reader integrated in the radio-phone-navigation system;
- hands free function via the radio speakers;
- microphone located in the front courtesy light;
- external aerial.
The integated radio-telephone-navigation system is a node in the CAN network, via which it exchanges information with the Body Computer and the other electronic control units.
The controls are shown on the integrated radio-telephone-navigation system display.
Some versions are equipped with a series of buttons on the steering wheel: these are used to send out radio and also phone commands.
Other control buttons are located in the front courtesy light.
The stylus aerial is fitted at the rear of the roof: this aerial has three functions (radio/ GSM/ GPS); as far as the telephone is concerned it is a GSM dual band reception aerial (GSM-ETACS at 900Hz and D.C.S. at 1800 Hz).
For more details on phone operation
See descriptions 5580P CONNECT PANEL [→939003540 5580P CONNECT PANEL]

## E3570 BUILT-IN RADIO PHONE - OPERATIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011703]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E35 RADIO ACCESSORIES > E3570 INTEGRATED RADIO PHONE > E3570 BUILT-IN RADIO PHONE - OPERATIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods; only with equipment: Connect Nav+
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011703

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
Radio P20 is supplied directly (pin 7 of connector A) from the battery via the line for fuse F23 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 .
The radio P20 receives an ignition-operated (INT) power supply (pin 4 of connector A) via the line for fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2 .
Pin 8 of connector A is earthed.
Pins 1 and 3 of connector A receive the CAN line by which radio P20 is connected to Body Computer M1 and the other system nodes.
The control buttons located on the front courtesy light G10 - connector G - are connected to pins 10 and 12 of connector D of P20.
The hands free microphone, also located in the front courtesy light G10 - connector D - is connected to pins 9 and 18 of connector F of P20.

## E3580 PROVISION FOR CELL PHONE - DESCRIPTION  [939011707]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E35 RADIO ACCESSORIES > E3580 PREPARATION FOR CELLULAR TELEPHONE > E3580 PROVISION FOR CELL PHONE - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011707

#### DESCRIPTION
The vehicle is available, on request, not equipped with a CONNECT NAV + system - it can be supplied with provision for installing a cell phone.
The system includes:
- connection for a cell phone;
- hands free function via the radio speakers;
- external GSM aerial;
- microphone located in the front courtesy light.
The connection for the telephone, located at the base of the centre console, includes all the power supplies and signals needed for the operation of the telephone.
The stylus aerial is fitted at the rear of the roof: it is a two-function aerial with two leads: one is the actual radio aerial used by the radio, one is the cable for the dual band reception telephone (GSM-ETACS at 900 Hz and D.C.S. at 1800 Hz).
The radio receives input audio signals from the telephone connection; the sound of the telephone always arrives at a fixed volume which can, however, be adjusted in the radio menu function.
The operation of the telephone switches off the radio temporarily (MUTE function).
The connection for the telephone has two power supplies; one direct and one with the ignition ON: the above two lines are protected by two fuses in the junction unit under the dashboard; there is also a power supply with the side lights on to light up the telephone
See E2535 CONTROL LIGHTS [→939002993]

## E3580 PROVISION FOR CELL PHONE - OPERATIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011708]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E35 RADIO ACCESSORIES > E3580 PREPARATION FOR CELLULAR TELEPHONE > E3580 PROVISION FOR CELL PHONE - OPERATIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011708

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The connection D75 receives the direct supply - pin 9 - from the battery via the line for fuse F39 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2 (this power supply "passes through" the Body Computer M1, pin 26 of connector H).
It receives an ignition-controlled power supply (INT) - pin 7 - via the line for fuse F49 of junction unit B2 .
The power supply with the side lights on reaches pin 8 coming from the Body Computer M1, pin 18 of connector H: the telephone, if fitted, is lit up like the other controls
See E2535 CONTROL LIGHTS [→939002993]
Pin 10 of connector D75 is earthed.
Pins 4 and 3 of D75 provide the audio signal (+ and - respectively) for the radio P20 - pins 7 and 8 of connector D, which then controls the speakers.
See E3510 RADIO [→939003053]
Pin 1 of D75 is also connected to the radio P20, pin 9 of connector D (MUTE function).
The hands free microphone located in the front courtesy light G10 - connector D - is connected to pins 5 and 6 of D75.

## E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL - DESCRIPTION  [939011718]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E40 INSTRUMENT PANEL > E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL > E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V, 2.4 JTD 20V; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011718

#### DESCRIPTION
The instruments currently on board the vehicle in question are composed of the main control panel located inside the steering wheel and a central instrument console in the middle of the dashboard. The main panel contains a large reconfigurable matrix LCD (HIGH version) or a negative contrast alphanumerical LCD (LOW version only).
There is also a buzzer and a brightness sensor inside the instrument panel for the automatic adjustment (daytime/nightime) of the brightness of the instrument panel lights.
See E2535 CONTROL LIGHTS [→939002993]
The centre instrument console consists of:
- fuel level gauge with reserve warning light
- engine coolant temperature gauge with overheating warning light
- turbo pressure gauge
The instrument panel is a CAN node through which information is exchanged with the Body Computer and with the other electronic units.
The centre module containing the three sets of instruments is not a B-CAN node, but is connected by means of a special serial line to the instrument panel node which sends the module all the signals necessary for the display of the required information.
- Speedometer: the function of the speedometer includes displaying the vehicle speed in the instrument panel: this information comes from the ABS control unit, via the Body Computer.
- Engine rpm: this function involves the display on the instrument panel of the engine rotation speed by means of the message sent via the CAN from the engine management control unit.
- Milometer: the milometer function includes the display and memorizing of the total and trip mileage: the journey information is processed by the Body Computer by means of a counter; the special button in the panel to the side of the steering wheel zeroes the trip meter.
- Fuel level: the Body Computer receives the signal from the sensor integrated in the pump assembly inside the fuel tank and processes it to guarantee suitable filtering/damping for the panel gauge, also managing the reserve warning light.
- Engine oil level: the function signals the status of the engine oil level at starting (for about 3 seconds) in the display. The actual instrument panel operates a hot wire oil level sensor. If the oil level is below the minimum value, the message "minimum oil level" is also sent.
- Brake pad wear state: this function involves the specific warning light coming on: the Body Computer detects the brake pad wear status when braking (signal from the brake pedal) in a prolonged manner (occasional signals are ignored).
- Handbrake applied: the warning light for the handbrake status is controlled by a specific switch; in addition, if a given speed level is exceeded in conjunction with this signal, a warning signal is activated: the signal is sent, via the CAN, from the Body Computer.
- Insufficient brake fluid: this function involves the "insufficient brake fluid level" warning light in the instrument panel coming on with the signal sent by the Body Computer via the CAN.
For more details
See descriptions 5560 INSTRUMENTS [→939003534 5560 INSTRUMENTS]
> Note: The operation of the warning lights which do not come under any other functions is illustrated below: the other warning lights and displays are described and illustrated in the diagrams for the components to which they refer.

## E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939011719]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E40 INSTRUMENT PANEL > E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL > E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: engines: 1.9 JTD 8V, 1.9 JTD 16V, 2.4 JTD 20V; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939011719

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The ignition-operated power supply (INT) for the instrument panel E50 reaches pin 1 of connector A via the line for fuse F37 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2; the direct power supply reaches pin 2 of connector A via the fuse line F53 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2; pin 7 of connector A is earthed (earth controlled by the Body Computer M1).
The instrument panel E50 is connected from pins 3 and 4 of connector A with the Body Computer M1 and via the latter to the entire CAN: the signal reaches the electronic speedometer (from the ABS control unit M50) via the CAN: the same signal is replicated by pin 16 of M50 at pin 7 of connector A of the Body Computer M1.
The electronic rev counter receives the engine rpm signal received from the engine management control unit M10 via the CAN.
The km reset button for the trip meter, located in the left panel H90, sends an earth signal to pin 7 of connector C of E50.
The fuel level gauge is controlled by means of signals coming from the level gauge located in the fuel pump assembly N40 - at pins 4 and 15 of connector D of the Body Computer M1 and from there via the CAN to the instrument panel E50.
The brake pad wear warning light is controlled on the basis of the signal that reaches pin 23 of connector B of the Body Computer M1 from the sensors for K20 and K21.
The insufficient brake fluid level/handbrake warning light is lit up by a signal from the handbrake switch I40 that reaches pin 14 of connector D of the Body Computer M1 or from the signal from the brake fluid level sensor K25 that reaches pin 18 of connector A of M1.
All these signals are transferred via the CAN to the instrument panel E50.
The engine oil level sensor K32 receives a power supply from the panel E50 from pin 17 of connector B and relays the signal to pin 18.
The centre module E20 is connected by means of a special serial line - from pin 1 - to the instrument panel node E50 pin 1 of connector C; the protected power supply reaches pin 3 of E20, whilst the reference earth reaches pin 2.
The dimmed power supply for the auxiliary instruments E20 leaves from pin 5 of connector C of E50.
See E2535 CONTROL LIGHTS [→939002993]

## E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL - DESCRIPTION  [939005802]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E40 INSTRUMENT PANEL > E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL > E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL - DESCRIPTION
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: engines: 1.8; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939005802

#### DESCRIPTION
The instruments currently on board the vehicle in question are composed of the main control panel located inside the steering wheel and a central instrument console in the middle of the dashboard. The main panel contains a large reconfigurable matrix LCD (HIGH version) or a negative contrast alphanumerical LCD (LOW version only).
There is also a buzzer and a brightness sensor inside the instrument panel for the automatic adjustment (daytime/nightime) of the brightness of the instrument panel lights.
See E2535 CONTROL LIGHTS [→939002993]
The centre instrument console consists of:
- fuel level gauge with reserve warning light
- engine coolant temperature gauge with overheating warning light
- engine oil temperature gauge with overheating warning light
The instrument panel is a CAN node through which information is exchanged with the Body Computer and with the other electronic units.
The centre module containing the three sets of instruments is not a B-CAN node, but is connected by means of a special serial line to the instrument panel node which sends the module all the signals necessary for the display of the required information.
- Speedometer: the function of the speedometer includes displaying the vehicle speed in the instrument panel: this information comes from the ABS control unit, via the Body Computer.
- Engine rpm: this function involves the display on the instrument panel of the engine rotation speed by means of the message sent via the CAN from the engine management control unit.
- Milometer: the milometer function includes the display and memorizing of the total and trip mileage: the journey information is processed by the Body Computer by means of a counter; the special button in the panel to the side of the steering wheel zeroes the trip meter.
- Fuel level: the Body Computer receives the signal from the sensor integrated in the pump assembly inside the fuel tank and processes it to guarantee suitable filtering/damping for the panel gauge, also managing the reserve warning light.
- Engine oil level: the function signals the status of the engine oil level at starting (for about 3 seconds) in the display. The actual instrument panel operates a hot wire oil level sensor. If the oil level is below the minimum value, the message "minimum oil level" is also sent.
- Engine coolant temperature gauge: is operated - via the instrument panel - by the special sensor on the engine. The maximum temperature warning light is controlled by a microprocessor when the value measured exceeds a certain limit.
- Brake pad wear state: this function involves the specific warning light coming on: the Body Computer detects the brake pad wear status when braking (signal from the brake pedal) in a prolonged manner (occasional signals are ignored).
- Handbrake applied: the warning light for the handbrake status is controlled by a specific switch; in addition, if a given speed level is exceeded in conjunction with this signal, a warning signal is activated: the signal is sent, via the CAN, from the Body Computer.
- Insufficient brake fluid: this function involves the "insufficient brake fluid level" warning light in the instrument panel coming on with the signal sent by the Body Computer via the CAN.
For more details
See descriptions 5560 INSTRUMENTS [→939003534 5560 INSTRUMENTS]
> Note: The operation of the warning lights which do not come under any other functions is illustrated below: the other warning lights and displays are described and illustrated in the diagrams for the components to which they refer.

## E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION  [939005803]
- Path: Electrical equipment > 1 ELECTRICAL FUNCTIONS > E40 INSTRUMENT PANEL > E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL > E4010 INSTRUMENT PANEL - FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
- Kind: functional description (how the circuit works)
- Applies to: engines: 1.8; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939005803

#### FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION
The ignition-operated power supply (INT) for the instrument panel E50 reaches pin 1 of connector A via the line for fuse F37 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2; the direct power supply reaches pin 2 of connector A via the fuse line F53 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2; pin 7 of connector A is earthed (earth controlled by the Body Computer M1).
The instrument panel E50 is connected from pins 3 and 4 of connector A with the Body Computer M1 and via the latter to the entire CAN: the signal reaches the electronic speedometer (from the ABS control unit M50) via the CAN: the same signal is replicated by pin 16 of M50 at pin 7 of connector A of the Body Computer M1.
The electronic rev counter receives the engine rpm signal received from the engine management control unit M10 via the CAN.
The km reset button for the trip meter, located in the left panel H90, sends an earth signal to pin 7 of connector C of E50.
The fuel level gauge is controlled by means of signals coming from the level gauge located in the fuel pump assembly N40 - at pins 4 and 15 of connector D of the Body Computer M1 and from there via the CAN to the instrument panel E50.
The brake pad wear warning light is controlled on the basis of the signal that reaches pin 23 of connector B of the Body Computer M1 from the sensors for K20 and K21.
The insufficient brake fluid level/handbrake warning light is lit up by a signal from the handbrake switch I40 that reaches pin 14 of connector D of the Body Computer M1 or from the signal from the brake fluid level sensor K25 that reaches pin 18 of connector A of M1.
All these signals are transferred via the CAN to the instrument panel E50.
The engine oil level sensor, incorporated in the temperature and level sensor K52, receives a power supply from the panel E50 from pin 17 of connector B and relays the signal to pin 18.
The engine oil temperature sensor K52 receives the reference earth from the panel E50 - pin 17 of connector D - and relays the signal to pin 18.
The centre module E20 is connected by means of a special serial line - from pin 1 - to the instrument panel node E50 pin 1 of connector C; the protected power supply reaches pin 3 of E20, whilst the reference earth reaches pin 2.
The dimmed power supply for the auxiliary instruments E20 leaves from pin 5 of connector C of E50.
See E2535 CONTROL LIGHTS [→939002993]
